Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to stay afloat as Fifa president after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England, Wales and other European nations have led the charge in officially withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027, while Uefa asserted that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands in a bid to oust him from power.

The global players union, Fifpro, have also turned on Infantino, accusing him of a “profound abuse of presidential power” in an explosive statement.

However, Infantino’s allies are beginning to surface, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president.

As dominoes continue to fall, here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:

Who has withdrawn its support for Infantino?

Uefa 🇪🇺

Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership, insisting that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands despite the sell-off scheme being scrapped.

It points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino ( PA )

Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

“The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Finland 🇫🇮

Finland kickstarted this process, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

Serbia 🇷🇸

The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden 🇸🇪

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists."

open image in gallery Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations ( PA )

Croatia 🇭🇷

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

"This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time."

Albania 🇦🇱

The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Greece 🇬🇷

The Greek federation similarly sent their withdrawal of support Fifa’s way.

Who is also opposing Infantino?

Concacaf (Confederation for North America and the Caribbean) 🌎

Concacaf have come out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election.

open image in gallery Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino ( Getty )

AFC (Asian Football Confederation) 🌏

The AFC was similarly aggrieved by the non-existent consultation from Fifa regarding the Infantino’s scheme, rejecting the proposal before calling on Fifa to undertake an “urgent review of its governance”.

Germany 🇩🇪

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board."

Denmark 🇩🇰

Denmark are in a similar position to Germany, having not endorsed Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal.

There is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”

Norway 🇳🇴

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation, and while they have not yet officially sent a letter to withdraw their support in him, such action is expected in the coming days.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

open image in gallery Lise Klaveness has called on Infantino to resign ( Reuters )

Netherlands 🇳🇱

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is also yet to officially withdraw its support but is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

Romania 🇷🇴

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) were among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset.

As a result, the FRF will withold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a new term, until further clarifications.”

Jordan 🇯🇴

Jordan are so far the only non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

Sierra Leone 🇸🇱

Former Sierra Leone FA president and ex-Fifa Council member Isha Johansen has indicated that Africa’s support of Infantino is not unanimous across the continent after emerging as one of the African voices opposing the privatisation project.

He urged African football chiefs to think carefully about the game’s future, saying: "What price does one have to pay in order to get to this elevated development for football in Africa?"

Canada 🇨🇦

Canada prime minister Mark Carney joined his UK counterpart Andy Burnham in calling for Infantino to be ousted from his position as president.

“It should be fatal,” Carney said, whose country co-hosted this summer’s World Cup. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr Infantino."

Who is supporting Infantino?

Caf (African Football Confederation) 🌍

Caf, the governing body for African football, has become the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino. Its 54 member associations account more than a quarter of Fifa’s 211 members.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Argentina 🇦🇷

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had thus far only expressed support of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Argentina president Javier Milei (left) behind Infantino at the "Board of Peace" hosted by US president Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Mexico 🇲🇽

Mexico joined Argentina from the Americas, breaking rank from the United States, Canada and the rest of Concacaf that had condemned Infantino’s plan and aligned itself against his leadership.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations."

Paraguay 🇵🇾

Paraguay has also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base begins to surface.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Qatar 🇶🇦

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the plan.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Qatar's FA has backed Infantino to continue as president ( Getty Images )

Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

"One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

Kuwait 🇰🇼

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”

Lebanon 🇱🇧

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

“Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he said, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

Indonesia 🇮🇩

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”

Philippines 🇵🇭

Philippines have also backed Infantino and backed for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Bhutan 🇧🇹

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Morocco 🇲🇦

The location of Infantino’s crisis meeting on Wednesday, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an important accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

open image in gallery Infantino held his crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco ( AP )

Egypt 🇪🇬

Similar to their north African counterpart, Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Mauritania 🇲🇷

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

Niger 🇳🇪

Same as above, with Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger coming out quickly in support of Infantino.

DR Congo 🇨🇩

DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support”. of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Nigeria 🇳🇬

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off plan.

Comoros 🇰🇲

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Said Ali Athouman, also backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”

open image in gallery A number of African nations have fallen in line with the stance of Caf president Patrice Motsepe ( Getty )

Malawi 🇲🇼

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, echoed the same concerns in his support for Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money."

Uganda 🇺🇬

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed Malawi’s sentiments, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

Gambia 🇬🇲

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

South Africa 🇿🇦

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

"Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too."

Who are yet to confirm a stance?

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has not publicly stated its position, though its biggest footballing nation New Zealand did come out in opposition to Infantino’s proposal.

Conmebol, the governing body for South America, also took a while to break its silence. It expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”. However, it is yet to reveal their stance on Infantino and has previously been very supportive of the incumbent president, with Conmebol pushing for a 64-team World Cup for the 2030 edition.

Poppy Oliver, the eldest daughter of chef Jamie Oliver, has announced her engagement to long-term boyfriend Ben Newman.

The 24-year-old’s mother, Jools Oliver, shared the news on Wednesday via Instagram, posting a photograph of Newman proposing on a beach.

Jools, whose real name is Juliette, wrote: “Our first baby Poppy Honey is getting married. We are so excited, proud and happy. Ben we all adore you.”

She revealed that the couple’s romance blossomed at university, where they were next-door neighbours.

Recalling their early days, Jools wrote: “Little did I know as we moved Pop into her second house at university, whilst I was sweating over your shoe rack flat pack, you seemed very distracted with the boy who had just moved in next door.

“Five years later you had met your soul mate. So excited for the next chapter.”

open image in gallery Poppy, 24, is a University of Leeds graduate ( Instagram )

Further posts on Jools’ Instagram included additional photos of the happy couple and a video of the Oliver family celebrating with balloons in their kitchen.

There was also a close-up of Poppy, whose full name is Poppy Honey Rosie Oliver, showcasing her engagement ring.

Oliver’s mother also commented on the video, stating: “Love this so much, it was such wonderful news, made me cry. Love them both.”

Jamie and Jools Oliver have been married for 26 years and are also parents to daughters Daisy Boo Pamela, 23, Petal Blossom Rainbow, 17, Buddy Bear Maurice, 15, and River Rocket, 10.

open image in gallery Poppy Oliver, right, with her mother Jools and brother Buddy ( Getty )

Oliver first rose to prominence with the BBC Two series The Naked Chef in 1999, later establishing a restaurant group that entered administration in 2019, and has authored more than 30 books.

Poppy was born in 2003, three years after her parents were married, and went to Channing School in Highgate before studying English at the University of Leeds.

When she graduated in 2023, her mother posted on Instagram, saying that the family had “never felt so proud”.

Poppy had struggled with reading as a young child, but went on to develop a “complete obsession with books, reading and writing”, her mother wrote.

After graduating in 2023, Poppy took a gap year in Australia, where she worked as a waitress in Sydney.

Even the Finns have to journey with purpose to get to the Savonlinna Opera Festival, which has been going strong for well over 100 years. There are Londoners who think that the trip down to East Sussex to Glyndebourne is a major outing, but Savonlinna requires a four hour train journey north-east from Helsinki: an intercity train followed by one of those two-carriage local things that trundle for the final leg through forests of pine and birch, with the occasional glimpse of lakes.

On the way the rails run parallel to the Russian border, at one point coming within a few hundred metres. That border is closed now, of course, and the festival no longer has the old influx of visitors from St Petersburg. They have been replaced by the British, Danes and Americans.

When the trees clear and Savonlinna appears, the view is breathtaking. Its 15th century castle dominates the lake, Finland’s largest. In the courtyard, covered for the season, opera plays to an audience of over 2000 for a month (this year 17 July to 9 August, in 2027 from 3 to 31 July). The programme is a mixture of the festival’s own productions, co-productions and each year a guest company from around the world. This year the guest was the company from the other end of the Baltic in Gothenburg.

The ensemble, orchestra and chorus proved to be among the finest. The performances they gave of Verdi’s La Traviata and Bellini’s Norma were not remnants of last season but previews of next, and Swedish audiences are in for a treat when the trucks arrive home. Both were musically triumphant. In Norma the title role was sung for the first time in her career by Lisette Oropesa. It requires a soprano at the peak of her powers and believable as a high priestess and young mother at the same time. So, at 42, Oropesa is perfect. This is one of the most vocally challenging roles in opera, but Oropesa has the range and agility to make those demands sound an entirely natural consequence of the libretto.

open image in gallery Honestly, wow: The city of Savonlinna in Finland ( Supplied )

She did not monopolise the singing honours though. Ann-Kristin Jones (fully Swedish despite the Welsh-looking surname) was Oropesa’s equal, singing Adalgisa, the younger priestess who unwittingly becomes her rival in loving their enemy Roman ruler. Jones is far less famous than she should be. Hers is a voice of power, blending with Oropesa’s with beauty in their duets. This was one of those rare evenings in opera when there were no weak links in the cast or orchestra. The stone walls of the castle act as natural amplifiers so the sound is huge.

Norma was acted but not staged at Savonlinna, unlike La Traviata the previous evening, which turned out to be a bonus. Acting Violetta in the Verdi was Venera Gimadieva, the same age as Oropesa but not singing the main role for anything like the first time. She is something of a specialist, having sung it first at Savonlinna in 2013, the next year at Glyndebourne, and in 2015 at Covent Garden. Not surprisingly she glides through the arias and knows just how to bring the audience’s focus on to her fatal struggle against consumption, whatever the frenzy around her. This was no easy task here, with director Silvia Paoli unable to resist cluttering the stage with unnecessary business: furniture movers wearing rabbit heads; chorus members inventing endless distractions; some particularly disruptive lighting. Luckily Gimadieva’s brilliance shone through and was matched by Yngve Søberg as the misguided and destructive Germont father, his magnificent baritone voice more often to be heard at Norwegian National opera.

The lure of Savonlinna is as much about the castle and its setting as the quality of the music. The first is unchanging and when the music-making is as fine as this, the experience is properly overwhelming. And then, after Norma, strolling back from the castle as the sun went down behind us at midnight and the full moon rose over the lake to the east, the fireworks crashed into the sky to mark Savonlinna’s 385th birthday as a city. I mean, honestly, wow!

Swallowing capsules containing human faeces from someone with no food allergies could help people with peanut allergies become more tolerant to the nut, a new study has suggested.

The trial, conducted by researchers at Boston Children’s Hospital, is the first evidence that faecal transplants – transferring gut bacteria from faecal samples of healthy donors – can be used to treat allergies.

The findings will be a boost to peanut allergy sufferers, with around two per cent of children in the UK believed to be affected.

Six people who were highly allergic to peanuts found that their reactions improved after a trial that used frozen “poop pills”, donated by people with healthy gut microbiomes to transfer good bacterialstrains into 10 young adults with severe peanut allergies who reacted to traces of the allergen.

open image in gallery A study by King’s College London in 2024 found regularly feeding children peanuts from infancy until the age of five reduced the rate of peanut allergy by 71 per cent (Katie Collins/PA) ( PA Archive )

After a one-time treatment of 36 pills taken each over few hours, three participants improved when tested four months later tolerating eating multiple peanuts.

In the next round of the study, participants took antibiotics before the fecal transplant to see if the donor bacteria transferred more successfully when it didn’t have to compete with the participants’ own resident gut microbes. Three of these five participants improved in peanut tolerance and ingested more than four peanuts before reacting, suggesting that the antibiotics did increase the efficiency of the microbiome transfer.

Researchers analysed blood samples from the research participants and found those who responded to the therapy had increased levels of bile salts, which break down fats for the small intestine to absorb, when compared to the people who didn’t respond. They suggested that the good bacteria from the faecal transplants was more adept at metabolising bile salts than the original bacteria, and it increased levels of immune regulatory cells that protect from allergic reactions.

Dr Talal Chatila, MD, director of translational immunology, explained that the right bacteria can help make the gut immune system of those with allergies more tolerant.

"Food allergy reflects a failure of oral tolerance, the process by which the gut immune system learns to accept food, and what this study shows is that the right bacteria can help restore that process, working through bile acid metabolites to promote the immune cells that enforce tolerance,” they said. “Knowing how the bacteria restore tolerance to food in allergic individuals allows us to optimize the therapy for more effective outcomes."

open image in gallery The prevalence of peanut allergies in young children has been increasing over decades

Dr Rima Rachid, director of the Food Allergy Program and the Allergen Immunotherapy Program, said: “This landmark study was the first to demonstrate that a microbiome-based therapy may improve food allergy in people while also revealing how gut bacteria, their metabolites, and the immune system work together to influence treatment response.”

“Larger studies of fecal and microbiota transplantation are now essential to confirm these findings, identify the patients most likely to benefit, and discover beneficial bacteria that could be developed into targeted probiotic therapies for food allergy.”

Peanut and tree nut allergies are the most commonly known foods to cause anaphylaxis, often developing in early childhood. In the past, certain antibody medications or small dose exposure immunotherapy were found to raise tolerance to a sensitive food, but allergic reactions soon returned once the therapy stops, meaning patents could still experience life-threatening reactions.

Dr Rachid hopes to lead a new study where teens will receive microbe transplantation therapy in collaboration with Alexander Khoruts, MD, of the University of Minnesota.

This newer therapy uses a purified concentrated form of microbes than the faecal pills that can be stored in a home refrigerator. Patients will take the capsules from home under medical supervision and undergo food challenges to evaluate for changes in their tolerance to peanut.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Rodri set to leave Man City, Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives, Man Utd done deal
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca who are in negotiations over a €45m fee.

Arsenal were dealt a blow in one of their summer transfer pursuits as Vinicius Jr has signed a contract extension with Real Madrid. The Gunners have moved on from targeting the winger and have reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez while PSG’s Bradley Barcola is also on their list.

In more positive news, Bruno Guimaraes has completed a medical at Arsenal ahead of his £75m move from Newcastle United. The 28-year-old midfielder is now expected to be announced as a new Gooner on Friday ahead of Arsenal’s pre-season fixtures this weekend. The deal represents a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal’s title defence.

Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have also lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola’s side. The European champions may be willing to let them go especially following Maghnes Akliouche signing from Monaco.

Elsewhere, Manchester United have added to their ranks by bringing in a teenage midfielder and they are exploring their options at left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

Sports.title: Man City set transfer price for Rodri with Barcelona way off valuation – after he picked them over Real Madrid move
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY will demand more than £60million if Rodri tells them he wants to join Barcelona this month.

The former Ballon d’Or winner is wanted by the Catalan giants who are preparing an opening offer in the region of £38million.



That is unlikely to tempt the Prem club to part with their World Cup winner – even though he only has 10 months remaining on his contract.

City’s stance has always been that if a player is clear that he wants to leave then they will not stand in his way.



Rodri’s agent told a Spanish television station that the midfielder had decided he wants a switch to the Nou Camp – despite previous interest from Real Madrid.

He was quoted as saying: “Out of respect for Madrid – as they have been class – Rodri has informed them his decision is to join Barca.”



But the club’s hierarchy – many of whom are here in Seoul for the second leg of their pre-season tour – have not been informed of that as things stand.

The 30-year-old is due back at the City Football Academy early next week to begin his preparations for the season.

However he underwent a minor back operation after the World Cup so that could put his return to training back a few days.

City are pushing on with their move for Lille’s £85m-rated youngster Ayyoub Bouaddi regardless of what happens with Rodri.

Sources at the Etihad have indicated that progress has been made over the Morocco World Cup star, 18, in recent days.

However if Rodri goes, then City are likely to look for a replacement – even though they have new boy Elliot Anderson and Nico Gonzalez already in that position.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer’s girlfriend stuns in blue athleisure tank top as Chelsea star’s sister gives rave review
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER’s girlfriend Olivia Holder was showered with compliments on her latest Instagram post.

Palmer’s sister, Hallie, was among those spreading the love as Holder posed outside a swanky doorway in London.

MARC CUCURELLA might be the name on everyone’s lips after inspiring Spain to their World Cup triumph this summer.

But his wife Claudia Rodriguez, 26, is catching attention too after another stunning display while on holiday.



Rodriguez is enjoying a break in Capri, Italy, with the Real Madrid star after his busy summer in the USA.

The influencer, posted a photodump showing off her holiday, including a stunning picture of herself in a low-cut black dress that showed off her cleavage.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso could let up to 25 Chelsea players leave including Enzo Fernandez and four strikers
Sports.content:
CHELSEA could still sell up to FIFTEEN players before the end of the summer transfer window, with a further TEN potentially moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan.

As ever at Chelsea, the end of the window is a busy time, but with most of their incoming signings sorted, the Blues have plenty of outgoings to work on.



There are several players who have been involved in various ‘bomb squads’ over the past few seasons who are in need of a permanent move, as well as a few top academy talents who need more regular minutes in adult football.

Playing only once a week this season is expected to help Xabi Alonso in terms of his adaptation and to help Chelsea in terms of their mission to qualify for Europe again.



But having a bloated squad, with several players unhappy about a lack of minutes won’t do Alonso’s squad harmony any good at all, so there are plenty of calls for head honcho Behdad Eghbali to be making in the next couple of weeks.

These are all the players who SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield thinks could be waving goodbye to Stamford Bridge before the window closes.



Filip Jorgensen

The Danish stopper is expected to complete a move to sister club Strasbourg very soon, in his bid for more regular minutes after a disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge.

Gaga Slonina

Has also been training with Strasbourg, as he looks to get his career back on track – multiple European clubs have shown an interest in the former Chicago Fire keeper.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Axel Disasi

Could be Crystal Palace‘s Maxence Lacroix replacement, after impressing on loan at West Ham in the back end of last season – a Premier League move is likely, though a handful of Serie A sides are reportedly interested.

Tosin Adarabioyo

Was Chelsea’s most experienced player last season, but has been underwhelming since joining on a free from Fulham, Xabi Alonso wants four or five centre-backs and he is not one of them.

Benoit Badiashile



Napoli looks the most likely option for him at the moment, with a potential loan with option to buy deal on the cards.



Trevoh Chalobah

About to complete a move to Cesc Fabregas‘ FC Como side, and could even face Arsenal in his first game next Wednesday.

Wesley Fofana

May end up staying with Chelsea needing to get rid of so many defenders, Barcelona and Roma have been linked with a move, but he might have one last shot at reviving his Blues career this season.



Malo Gusto



PSG have been linked with a move for the versatile Frenchman, with Chelsea demanding £75m for his services. The arrival of Marco Palestra may spell the end of him at Stamford Bridge.



Romeo Lavia

Yet to complete 90 minutes for Chelsea, with AS Monaco reportedly interested in the Belgian midfielder. Has all the talent and ability in the world, but his injury record has made him a liability with Alonso needing players he can depend on.



Enzo Fernandez

Flirted with a move to Real Madrid in the summer, only for Los Blancos to put out a statement rejecting him. Finds himself in transfer limbo, with the club demanding £120 million for his sale and no serious suitors.



David Datro Fofana

How he is still a Chelsea player is ridiculous, as the club have been trying to sell him for what feels like forever – he could still be a Chelsea player three years from now, with his contract expiring in 2029.



Pedro Neto

There is no desperation for Chelsea to sell probably their best winger last season, though Manchester City are interested in the Portuguese man and the Blues would let him go for the right price – which is £70million.

Liam Delap

The second of FOUR out and out strikers on this list, after Fofana. Nottingham Forest, Everton, Leeds and Newcastle United have all been linked with him, though none seem close to agreeing a deal with Chelsea at the moment.



Nicolas Jackson

Chelsea want £65million for the Senegalese front man, with multiple clubs from the Premier League showing interest, and plenty from around Europe too.

Marc Guiu

Subject to one of the most bizarre transfer saga’s of the season this time last year, being brought back from his loan at Sunderland. Chelsea now have more promising strikers who are younger than him, so it makes sense to look for a permanent sale.



Players who could be loaned:

Denner Evangelista

Just joined on a 7-year contract and is a highly rated 18-year-old – it’s unclear what Chelsea plan to do with him for now, but you would imagine a loan makes the most sense.

Ishe Samuels Smith

Spent last season on loan at Swansea after bizarrely permanently joining Strasbourg and then re-joining Chelsea 33 days later. Another who could move permanently if not on loan.

Aaron Anselmino



Had a really promising loan at Borussia Dortmund last season which was cut short by the Blues, could do with more top European experience on loan this season.

Josh Acheampong

Not considered for sale by Chelsea, but needs minutes in the Premier League that he likely won’t get at Stamford Bridge having been sparsely used in pre-season so far.

Omari Kellyman



Had a successful loan at Cardiff last season, which the Blues may look to replicate this season.

Dastan Satpayev

The 17-year-old has technically still not joined Chelsea just yet, joining their pre-season tour as a “triallist”. Already has Champions League experience, and might be a shock candidate to stay at Stamford Bridge and get a few minutes as a backup, but if not, a loan move makes sense.

Mykhailo Mudryk

His shock return has left Chelsea with a decision to make.



A permanent sale would seem hasty, with it being more likely that he will either be slowly re-integrated, or more likely loaned out to another Premier League club or sister club Strasbourg.

Shim Mheuka

In need of a loan after proving he is too good for under-21s football last season, alongside Jesse Derry – multiple EFL clubs are interested, with a Championship move feeling the most likely.

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen



A season long loan to Portsmouth seems the most likely route to minutes for Chelsea’s Rio Ngumoha replacement, after he shone for the under-21s last season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Reggie Walsh

Multiple Championship clubs are thought to be interested in the midfielder who was Enzo Maresca‘s prodigal son in his time at Stamford Bridge – he has beefed up over the summer and could be a real hit in the Championship if the move is right.

Sports.title: 10 people who probably won’t be invited to Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez’s wedding including Wayne Rooney
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO and Georgina Rodriguez are set to tie the knot in Madeira this weekend.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner and his glamorous long-term partner have booked out a cathedral for the ceremony in Funchal and the five-star Savoy Palace hotel for the reception.



It promises to be one of the biggest celebrity weddings of the year – and invites will be hard to come by.

So those who have got on the wrong side of CR7 over the course of his career will no doubt be left off the guest list.



Here, SunSport takes you through 10 of Ronaldo‘s foes who almost definitely will NOT be there to watch him and Georgina get hitched…

Wayne Rooney

He formed a devastating partnership with Ronaldo at Manchester United in the mid-to-late 2000s, but these two are not best pals.



It all started when Ronaldo campaigned for Rooney to get sent off at the 2006 World Cup before winking at the bench.

Rooney then criticised Ronaldo during his second stint at United between 2021 and 2022, prompting the Portuguese to call his former team-mate ‘jealous’ during an interview with Piers Morgan.

He also said he was ‘better looking’ than Wazza, too!

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Lionel Messi

The two Ballon d’Or titans have gone toe-to-toe for GOAT supremacy over the past two decades.

And theirs is a relationship built on respect rather than closeness.

Legends of Real Madrid and Barcelona can only become so friendly after all.

And with Messi winning the popular vote – with eight Ballon d’Or titles to Ronaldo’s five and a World Cup triumph on his CV – he probably won’t be making the jaunt to Madeira this weekend.

Erik ten Hag

A huge bust-up with Ten Hag spelled the end of Ronaldo’s second stint at Old Trafford.



The Portuguese threw a strop after being dropped by the then-United boss and refused to come on as a late substitute against Tottenham in 2022.

He then publicly stated he had ‘no respect’ for Ten Hag, and his contract was terminated by mutual consent.

Ralf Rangnick

Ronaldo did not seem overly impressed with the German when he took interim charge of United in 2021.

He admitted he had ‘never even heard of him’ and was not keen on his pressing tactics, according to reports.



Jamie Carragher

The Liverpool legend was adamant that United had made a mistake by re-signing Ronaldo.

And CR7 had evidently been paying attention, as when Sky Sports rocked up to Old Trafford in the summer of 2022, he warmly greeted former United team-mates Roy Keane and Gary Neville on the touchline before completely IGNORING Carragher. Brutal.

Gary Lineker

A staunch member of the pro-Messi brigade, Lineker is not convinced by Ronaldo’s claim to being the greatest footballer of all time.

And after making those feelings known, Ronaldo unfollowed him on social media.



Lineker told The Rest Is Football: “He doesn’t like me very much, Cristiano Ronaldo. I didn’t upset him by anything I said about him. Other than the fact I’m honest and think overall Messi’s a better footballer.”

Alessandro Florenzi

The former Italy and AC Milan star clashed with Ronaldo during a match in 2019.

Florenzi, who played for Roma at the time, gave then-Juventus star Ronaldo some stick for playing on while there was a man down injured.

Ronaldo then shushed Florenzi and mocked his height. But he was left with a bitter taste after Florenzi scored the opener in a 2-0 Roma win.



Casemiro

Having shared a dressing room with Ronaldo at Real Madrid and United, some might have fancied Casemiro as a shoo-in to make the wedding guest list.

But the Brazilian may have been struck off following his recent comments about Messi.

After joining him at Inter Miami, Casemiro said: “For me, without a doubt, I am coming to play with the best player of all time. He’s one of, if not the god of football.”

Antonio Cassano

Italian football legend and former Real Madrid star Cassano was highly critical of Ronaldo during his time at Juve.



He called him ‘selfish’ and insisted he ‘did not know how’ to play as part of a team.

Cassano later revealed that Ronaldo got hold of his phone number, messaged him about his football achievements and demanded more respect.

Sepp Blatter

The former Fifa boss made fun of Ronaldo during a speech at the Oxford Union in 2013, saying he spent ‘more time at the hairdresser’ than Messi.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ronaldo posted the clip publicly and Blatter lodged a formal apology with his club at the time, Real Madrid.

But we don’t expect that’ll be enough for the disgraced Swiss to get an invite this weekend.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate reveals how he spent World Cup as former England manager says ‘a lot has happened’
Sports.content:
GARETH SOUTHGATE has offered a glimpse into how he spent his first World Cup since resigning as England boss.

The former Three Lions manager, 55, chose to stay out of the public eye during the tournament and rejected punditry roles as he thought it might harm the team’s chances of victory.



England were knocked out in a semi-final defeat by Argentina which opened Southgate’s successor, Thomas Tuchel, up to fierce criticism.

Southgate, who was still on the touchline when England went to the quarter-finals in Qatar four years ago, watched the North American tournament from afar.



Although it wasn’t that far, as part of the Instagram slideshow he posted on Thursday featured snaps from New York.

The pictures were captioned: “A lot has happened over the past couple of months, mixing business with pleasure.



“I’ve had the chance to meet some incredible people, work on some exciting projects, and, most importantly, enjoy some quality downtime with the family. Grateful for it all!”

Southgate’s snaps included him taking in applause from the Royal Box at Wimbledon and posing on the corner of a Manhattan street.

He was also seen giving a motivational talk on stage, enjoying a drink in the exclusive Harvard Club and chatting with Prince William.

It was quite a change of pace from the way Southgate spent some of his summers during eight years in charge of England.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Southgate was linked with a handful of high-profile jobs after stepping down in 2024 following England’s second consecutive defeat in a Euros final.

But he suggested last year that his career as a head coach is probably over.



He told BBC Radio 4: “I’ve had one of the most incredible jobs in football which also had a higher purpose because it was my country.

“That’s going to be very hard to replicate. Having had 37 years in football I’m enjoying finding other areas where I think I might be able to make a difference.”

Sports.title: Man Utd clash against hated rivals free to air on ITV and could see Rashford return for first time in nearly two years
Sports.content:
TWO England World Cup stars could make their Manchester United returns on Wednesday in one of the country’s fiercest grudge matches.

The Red Devils’ clash against Leeds could have an additional spark if Marcus Rashford plays his first Man Utd game since 2024.



Rashford and Mainoo are set to arrive at the club’s Irish training camp on August 10 ahead of the rivalry soaked encounter at Dublin‘s Croke Park.

The England pair have been recuperating for three weeks as per Fifa recommendations after the Three Lions’ third place finish at the World Cup.



If Rashford does appear in the heated fixture – which will be free to air on ITV – it would complete one of the most remarkable homecomings in recent football history.

The 28-year-old last played for Man Utd over 600 days ago.



After making 25 goal contributions for Barcelona last season and repeatedly saying he wanted to remain with the LaLiga champions, Rashford’s future away from Old Trafford seemed certain.

However, the Catalan giants refused to trigger Rashford’s relatively modest £26m release clause, and no other team has been willing to entertain his lucrative wage bill as of yet.

Despite spending the past year and a half out on loan, Rashford remains the Red Devil’s highest earner, netting a lucrative £325k a week.

The England winger’s relationship with his boyhood club blew up in the winter of 2024-25.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A high profile rift with Ruben Amorim led the then manager to declare he would rather play a 63-year-old goalkeeping coach over Rashford.

However, the forward has fonder memories of current coach Michael Carrick.

Rashford scored 32 times during two and a half seasons alongside club legend Carrick, and there will be hopes he can start a fresh chapter under his former teammate.

Man Utd’s feisty preseason fixture against Leeds will be the first football match at 82,000 capacity Croke Park in over a decade.
