Sports.title: Arsenal lead £73m race for new striker target, 21, after Vinicius Jr snub but face Man Utd transfer competition
Sports.content:
ARSENAL and Manchester United could go head to head in a transfer battle for Inter Milan powerhouse Pio Esposito.

SunSport can reveal the Premier League giants had scouts at Inter’s pre-season derby with AC Milan in Perth to run the rule over the 21-year-old, who Inter value at £73million.



And the 6ft 3in striker passed his big-stage exam with flying colors — prompting glowing scouting reports to land straight on the desks of Mikel Arteta and Michael Carrick.

SunSport understands Gunners coaches have been monitoring the Italy international for months, with Arteta is keen on adding more attacking options behind Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz.



Gabriel Jesus is likely to leave with interest from AC Milan and other clubs in Italy, while the Gunners missed out on a landmark transfer for Vinicius Jr when he agreed new terms with Real Madrid.

Arteta wants a physically dominant focal point who can bully Prem centre-backs while working his socks off for the team — and Esposito is seen to fit that blueprint.



United meanwhile are also understood to have been tracking the striker for some time, but have no intention of rushing into an offer.

Red Devils chiefs have compiled an extensive dossier on Esposito, but feel there is no immediate emergency to slap a formal bid on the table right now.

The Old Trafford side are willing to sanction Joshua Zirkzee’s exit and want another striker behind Benjamin Sesko, but are likely to wait for Inter to soften their stance.

The San Siro side have publicly declared Esposito “untouchable” in a desperate bid to ward off English suitors from their golden boy.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But SunSport can exclusively reveal the Italian giants have privately set a price tag of around £73m through intermediaries.

Esposito is currently keeping his head down and refuses to throw his toys out of the pram or force a dramatic exit from San Siro.

However, sources close to the player reveal he is deeply seduced by the pull of the Premier League and remains wide open to a dream move to England if either titan makes a move.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate
Sports.content:
'Bribery', a boycott and a grovelling apology. Just an ordinary week in the life of Gianni Infantino.

The FIFA president may have backed down on his controversial plan to sell off the World Cup, but he remains in his position. After all, Infantino was in charge of 'the greatest World Cup of all time' and 'the greatest human, social and cultural event that mankind has ever witnessed and seen'.

According to him, anyway. Still, UEFA are planning to boycott FIFA competitions after its 55 members unanimously voted to do so, firmly opposing Infantino's plan that would've seen private investors buy the World Cup and other tournaments.

Outside of Europe, though, it's a different story. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) gave its backing to Infantino on Thursday - a rare boost to the under-fire Swiss chief.

‌



And CAF isn't alone in its support. However, it'll be the 211 individual nations who'll vote to decide Infantino's future if or when he goes up for re-election in March 2027, not the federations.

Let's breakdown who's for backing and who's for sacking Infantino.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Fight to oust shameless Gianni Infantino is just starting - UEFA must not let up READ MORE :

UEFA standing firm (55 votes)

Starting with Infantino's most powerful opposition, the European football governing body isn't letting up on their stance. There've been tensions between the two organisations for years, with UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin notably not attending last month's World Cup final, despite a European nation (Spain) being involved.

‌



On Thursday, UEFA announced that its boycott still stands in a strong-worded statement. And, as of now, all 55 nations are unlikely to vote for Infantino regardless of their previous support.

"UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions," the statement read. "First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's [Wednesday] announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

‌



England's Football Association has already withdrawn its support for Infantino's re-election. It joined the FAs of Wales, Serbia, Sweden, Finland and Norway in publicly going against him.

Should Gianni Infantino be allowed to continue? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images The relationship between Aleksander Ceferin and Gianni Infantino is strained (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Question marks over Asia (46 votes)

With 46 associations, the Asian Football Confedeation boasts the third-largest contingent of countries within FIFA. It joined UEFA in criticising Infantino's plan, having previously been in support of the 56-year-old and pledging to vote for him next year.

‌



However, AFC President Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa wrote in a letter to its members: "The AFC notes with great concern and disappointment that it was not consulted by FIFA at any level prior to the public announcement of this proposal, and nor has it received any detailed governance, financial or legal analysis of the proposal and its potential repercussions, which is totally unacceptable.

"Furthermore, the AFC is deeply concerned that FIFA's unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of continental football, which are based on solidarity, cooperation and transparency. Moreover, such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the confederations, which is not the case now."

Now that the plan has been scrapped, though, could Infantino rekindle his support from Asia? The Jordan FA certainly won't be voting for him.

Its president, Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, accused FIFA of 'bribery' this week before belatedly receiving funds that should've been available eight months ago. However, Prince AIi and Jordan's stance on Infantino remains, saying: "While this is a good development for our players, it does not change the serious concerns we in the football world have regarding the FIFA leadership, nor does it change what our FAs have been subjected to in the past.

‌



"It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the FIFA presidential elections. And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of FIFA: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him."

View 5 Images Prince Ali bin Hussein of Jordan has vowed not to vote for Gianni Infantino (Image: David Ramos - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

CONCACAF divided (35 votes)

Within CONCACAF - the confederation which represents North America, Central America and the Caribbean - there's already division. CONCACAF declared a loss of confidence in Infantino last week by saying that it was 'deeply concerned by the lack of due process' regarding the sell-off plan, calling for a 'comprehensive reckoning' over FIFA's leadership.

However, 2026 World Cup co-hosts Mexico appear to have broken rank and has thrown its support behind Infantino. In a statement, the Mexican Football Federation (FMF) declared: "The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defense lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it," the FMF said.

‌



"Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by President Infantino on August 5, 2026, to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

"The FMF supports President Infantino's leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening."

Prior to Infantino's climbdown, it was reported that CONCACAF's 41 members were considering withdrawing their letters of support for his re-election. Could Mexico's stance be a catalyst for support?

Should Gianni Infantino resign from FIFA? Have your say after scathing UEFA attack READ MORE :

CAF back Infantino (54 votes)

It's important to remember that despite the widespread backlash, Infantino still has friends dotted around the world. Africa will be a key player in next year's election and he can seemingly count on a huge 54 votes from the continent.

‌



CAF president Patrice Motsepe stated on Thursday that the federation welcomed FIFA's apology and will back Infantino. "For us in Africa, adherence to governance, due process and transparency is crucial and non-negotiable," Motsepe added.

"We are committed to continue working together with FIFA, its Member Associations, other Football Confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process and transparency."

Motsepe previously affirmed: "I personally support Gianni Infantino. He's not just a good friend, he's a loyal friend. He's loyal to Africa. I come from a background where when people have been loyal to you, you never stab them in the back."

View 5 Images Patrice Motsepe says that Gianni Infantino has the support of CAF (Image: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Argentina take stance after CONMEBOL indecision (10 votes)

With 10 members, the confederation for South American football is the smallest by number, although it boasts some of the most prestigious nations in the sport. And in good news for Infantino, CONMEBOL released a statement on Thursday confirming that it won't back a vote to oust him - although it was hardly a glowing endorsement.

It read: "Football belongs to everyone. Its future can only be built on the basis of respect for institutional governance, sound governance and the democratic procedures that represent FIFA's 211 Member Associations.

"On 18 November 2026, the deadline for submitting candidacies for the FIFA Presidency will expire. Thereafter, the FIFA Congress will elect, through the votes of its 211 Member Associations, the person who will lead the organisation during the next term, including overseeing the organisation of the FIFA Centennial World Cup 2030.

"Accordingly, CONMEBOL will not support any action or procedure that disregards or departs from those institutional mechanisms. The CONMEBOL Council calls for preserving the unity of the football family, acting with institutional responsibility, strengthening dialogue and fully respecting the mechanisms of governance. Because, above all differences, football comes first."

‌



It's important to note that three CONMEBOL nations - Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay - are co-hosting the 2030 World Cup, staging one game each before the tournament moves to its primary hosts: Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Argentina have also offered Infantino their backing in a lengthy statement.

View 5 Images Gianni Infantino can count on support from Argentina (Image: Alex Pantling - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent," it began.

"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

‌



Oceania set for talks (11 votes)

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) will hold talks to decide its position on Wednesday, August 12. As revealed by GB News, the meeting will involve the 11 members who came up the OFC - New Zealand, American Samoa, the Cook Islands, Fiji, New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tahiti, Tonga and Vanuatu.

New Zealand Football boss Andrew Pragnell called for unity among the OFC earlier this week. "There's obviously more power in numbers .... Certainly it helps when a confederation acts in unison," Pragnell told Reuters after praising FIFA for its commercial efforts while reiterating that 'governance is governance'.

"You've seen in some confederations, even in the last week, members go different ways from other members. At the end of the day, the independence of each member association is respected as well."

Mirror Football's verdict

Gianni Infantino is going nowhere - at least for now. While countries and federations consider their positions, UEFA still have another card to play in what it believes is the fight to save football: a vote of no confidence.

‌



That can be triggered via an extraordinary congress at any time, potentially ousting Infantino before his re-election bid.

And, of course, there's the nuclear outcome: UEFA delivering on their promise to boycott FIFA tournaments. Should that happen, it's unfathomable that Infantino can continue, even until next year's elections.

A more realistic outcome would be an alternative candidate emerging in the coming months.

Paris Saint-Germain's Nasser al-Khelaifi, who's also chairman of the association of European Football Clubs, could be a popular choice given his friendships in the game, while the aforementioned Prince Ali has stood for FIFA president before.

‌



However, CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani is seen as the frontrunner. Montagliani has been praised for cleaning up the confederation following allegations of corruption and financial problems, and he helped bring the World Cup to his beloved Canada.

A FIFA President being liked by football fans? Imagine that...

Sports.title: Man Utd legend's blazing row with staff at local tip – 'I'm banned now'
Sports.content:
Man Utd legend's blazing row with staff at local tip – 'I'm banned now'

Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt was left fuming when he was stopped from entering his local tip in his Range Rover

View 2 Images Nicky Butt has addressed the incident that led to him being banned from his local recycling centre

Nicky Butt has been kicked out of his local tip after a 'raging row' with workers. Butt, one of the Class of 92, blew his top when staff branded his Range Rover a commercial vehicle because the seats were folded flat. He dumped his 'smelling bags' anyway, prompting an employee to sprint after him.

‌



According to The Sun, Butt said: "There's this guy at the gate bit, and he flags me down and goes, 'Put your windows down I need to look in the back of your car'. I'm going, 'What for?'

‌



"I've got a lot of crap from the house, bit of cardboard... I missed the bin man last week, so I've got a few smelly bags.

‌



OPINION Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join by Abbie Meehan

Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero READ MORE :

"So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I'm not going in because it's a commercial van.

"So I'm raging, literally. I'm putting a bit of cardboard in the tip."

‌



Butt also claimed he was told he was 'sneaking' rubbish into the tip due to the blacked out windows on his Range Rover.

He added: "I thought, well, I'm there now, I'm gonna go for it. So I've got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up...

"Trying to chase me up the hill, but he's got his walkie-talkie out.

‌



View 2 Images Nicky Butt was a key member of Sir Alex Ferguson's squad that won the Treble in 1999 (Image: Mirrorpix)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"So I've literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I'm going back down the hill, and he's going mad at me.

‌



"Anyway, I'm banned from the tip."

Butt was a vital cog in the United machine throughout the 1990s, collecting six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League before his switch to Newcastle in 2004.

He remained at St James' Park for another six years, which included a loan spell at Birmingham City, before calling time on his playing career following a stint in China.

Article continues below

Since retiring, he has taken on various positions at United and owned a share in Salford City, where he served as CEO between 2022 and 2024.

Sports.title: England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub
Sports.content:
England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub

Ivan Toney, who represented England at this summer's World Cup, has been charged with assault following a police investigation into an incident at a Soho nightclub last year

View 2 Images Ivan Toney has been charged with assault (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

Ivan Toney has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following an incident at a Soho nightclub in December last year.

The England striker, 30, was charged on July 31 relating to the alleged assault on December 2025 on Wardour Street, London. He is due to appear in court on September 24.

A statement from the Met Police said: "A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

"Ivan Toney, 30 (16.03.1996), of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

"He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

"The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1."

Article continues below

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

Toney was part of England's squad at the recent World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico. He helped the Three Lions to a third-placed finish, their best performance since 1966.

His selection came as something of a surprise to many and attracted widespread criticism due to Toney playing his football in Saudi Arabia, despite plundering 42 goals last term.

Toney didn't feature until the semi-final defeat by Argentina, where he came on as a late substitute. But he started the third-place playoff win against France, playing 78 minutes.

Toney began his career with hometown club Northampton before signing for Newcastle in 2015. From there, he went out on loan to Barnsley, Shrewsbury, Scunthorpe and Wigan.

View 2 Images Toney played twice for England at the World Cup (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

It was at Peterborough where his goal-scoring form first caught the eye, leading to a move to Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals in 141 appearance for the Bees before his money-spinning Saudi switch, including 36 in the Premier League, leading to a first England call-up in 2022 and a debut in March 2023.

In all, Toney has played 10 times for his country, scoring once in a friendly against Belgium at Wembley in March 2024.

Sports.title: Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future
Sports.content:
Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future

Real Madrid were long considered the favourites to sign Rodri before Barcelona entered the running, with the midfielder having entered the final 12 months of his contract at Manchester City

View 2 Images Rodri has decided his next club (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Rodri's agent has announced that the Manchester City star wants to join Barcelona over arch rivals Real Madrid. Rodri, 30, agreed personal terms with Barca on Thursday in a sudden and dramatic twist.

‌



The Spaniard had been in talks with Real for weeks after suggesting back in March that he was keen on a move to the Bernabeu. But Barcelona have hijacked the move after Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director Deco and was convinced to join the La Liga champions.

‌



Although City haven't given up hope of tying Rodri down to a new contract after he entered the final year of his current deal, Etihad chiefs are well aware of his desire to return to Spain. In a late-night interview with Cadena SER, Rodri's agent, Pablo Barquero, revealed all.

‌



"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero told the Spanish radio station.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition READ MORE :

Barcelona are in the market for a midfielder after Frenkie de Jong was ruled out for several months. Rodri is seen as a plug and play option, having gotten over his injury troubles and helped Spain win the World Cup last month.

‌



The 30-year-old also picked up the Golden Ball at the tournament, playing an integral role for Luis de la Fuente's side. His departure from City would follow that of manager Pep Guardiola, defender John Stones and midfielder Bernardo Silva in a summer of change at the Etihad.

New boss Enzo Maresca remains desperate to keep him, though, and stated earlier this week: "It's very important (to have him). Any manager in the world wants Rodri because he's a top player; so it's important for me, the club and for everyone."

Should Manchester City sell Rodri? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Rodri was named Player of the Tournament at the World Cup (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

But Maresca's hopes could soon be dashed. Barcelona have room in their wage budget following the departure of Robert Lewandowski and appear to have enough funds to tempt City to the negotiating table, having bid around £100m for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez in June.

Rodri has spent seven years with City, winning four Premier League titles, one Champions League and two FA Cups. The former ex-Villarreal man received the Ballon d'Or in 2024, having won that year's European Championship with Spain.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has not yet followed transfer instructions previously laid out by Paul Scholes

View 4 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was told by a former team-mate to sell some players (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has not sanctioned any major sales so far this summer at Manchester United. This is despite United hero Paul Scholes recommending eight stars be sold.

‌



Carrick is currently taking charge of his first pre-season and there are just a few weeks until the Premier League returns. With only three first-team signings made so far in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, more additions are expected.

‌



However, there has yet to be a major exit from the club, aside from Casemiro's departure. In April, Scholes was asked for a series of United stars who were surplus to requirements and of the eight players he listed, only one appears set to leave as things stand.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee was among the players that Scholes believed should be sold and the former Bologna forward is edging closer to a return to Italy. La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee is willing to join Juventus, who are pursuing a loan arrangement with an option to buy.

View 4 Images Zirkzee could be on the move soon (Image: Getty)

‌



Scholes and Carrick spent seven seasons together in United's midfield during their playing days. However, whilst the pundit's suggestion to move on Zirkzee may materialise, the other seven stars Scholes mentioned could all remain part of United's squad next term, with Carrick's response clear.

The 51-year-old stressed the importance of United revamping their defence. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, Scholes said of Leny Yoro: "I think he's struggled, me. I think there's something in there, I think he needs a bit of time, but if you had to make a choice now, I'd probably sell him."

He also argued that the shift away from ex-boss Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back system would have implications for Noussair Mazraoui. Mazraoui has been linked with a departure this summer, though he remains part of Carrick's side. Highly-rated defender Yoro has also expressed a desire to make his mark at United next season.

‌



View 4 Images Yoro was a surprise inclusion (Image: Getty)

Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Turning to midfield, Scholes felt Manuel Ugarte would depart and the Uruguayan was linked with a move before picking up an injury at the World Cup. Mason Mount also featured on Scholes' eight-man list, though the England international has caught the eye during pre-season.

‌



Additionally, Scholes felt the moment had arrived to say goodbye to Harry Maguire, who continues to have a key role at United. He said: "I'm thinking about a Manchester United team you want to win the league and the Champions League and that's where United should be aiming. I'm not sure you'd do that with Maguire."

Elsewhere, United have held an interest in Newcastle United full-back Lewis Hall in the transfer window. Focusing on the left-back position, Scholes previously urged the club to offload long-serving Luke Shaw due to doubts about his reliability, despite him having featured in every Premier League fixture last season. He was equally prepared to let Patrick Dorgu leave.

View 4 Images Mount, Shaw and Maguire were three of the players that Scholes named (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Scholes said on Dorgu: "They brought him in as a wing-back and he's not really played much there. I'd probably sell. I'm not sure what position he is. Again, if you keep him then he's just a squad player."

Overall, of the eight players Scholes recommended be sold, only Zirkzee appears set for an imminent exit. There has been little speculation regarding the remaining seven of Yoro, Mazraoui, Shaw, Dorgu, Mount, Ugarte and Maguire.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has plenty on his plate as the Premier League champions bid to kick on this summer

View 4 Images Andrea Berta has a lot on his plate as Arsenal's sporting director (Image: Getty)

Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta has overseen some important signings since joining the club, with more expected to follow. But sales have been a challenge for the Gunners, with the problem persisting long before the Italian took up the role.

‌



The north London side's record sale still sits at just £35million. To put that into context, only three of the other 19 Premier League sides - Sunderland, Hull and Coventry - have lower records. Arsenal simply aren't selling well.

‌



A total of three sales this summer have raised less than £40m combined, with Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard completing permanent exits. Arsenal have already paid in the region of £34m for both Piero Hincapie and Christos Tzolis, whilst the anticipated move for Bruno Guimaraes will see them more than double their outlay.

‌



When it comes to record sales, it's telling that the top four spots are occupied by transfers from the Arsene Wenger era, and the club simply aren't keeping up with the big-money exits that clubs like Chelsea and Manchester City sanction. Here are their 10 most lucrative offloadings, in reverse order, per Transfermarkt figures.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

10. Joe Willock (£25.2m)

Willock's move to Newcastle was a case of striking whilst the iron was hot. The midfielder scored eight goals during a loan spell at St James' Park, driving up his value and convincing Arsenal to cash in.

‌



The England Under-21 international hasn't yet matched that goal tally across more than 100 games as a permanent Newcastle player, though his role became far less attacking under Eddie Howe. He was used sparingly last term, struggling to displace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

9. Eddie Nketiah (£25.4m)

Another recent sale, Nketiah demonstrated Premier League pedigree in an Arsenal shirt when he scored a hat-trick against Sheffield United in 2023. Months later, Crystal Palace took the plunge with a big-money bid and the striker - battling with the likes of Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus for opportunities - decided to try his luck elsewhere.

View 4 Images Nketiah is about to embark on his third season at Crystal Palace (Image: Getty)

‌

Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Arsenal have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, said to incorporate classic Arsenal design features that tie into the club's heritage.

The Eagles could end up paying even more for the England international if conditions for add-ons are met. However, his second season at Selhurst Park was cut short by injury and he will hope for a fresh start under new boss Pierre Sage.

8. Folarin Balogun (£25.7m)

Balogun, like Nketiah, moved in search of more regular first-team football. Again, Arsenal got good money for a fringe player when he followed up a 21-goal Ligue 1 season at Reims with a move to their rivals Monaco.

‌



The United States international top-scored for his club last term and thrived for his country at the World Cup. There's no guarantee he would have developed at the same speed in North London, though.

7. Alex Iwobi (£26m)

Academy graduate Iwobi grew into his role at Arsenal, scoring in the 2019 Europa League final defeat to Chelsea and playing 100 league games for the Gunners. But the arrival of Nicolas Pepe meant he was considered disposable.

Marco Silva signed the Nigerian international for Everton but was gone within months in a tough first season. Things have gone better for Iwobi after a reunion with Silva at Fulham, where he has thrived in a deeper midfield role than the one he occupied at his boyhood club.

‌



6. Robin van Persie (£26.3m)

View 4 Images Van Persie's United move was one of 2012's most talked-about transfers (Image: Getty)

The £26m paid by Manchester United for Van Persie in 2012 was worth a great deal more then than now. Still, it's telling that a deal from more than a decade ago is one of the top 10 on this list. And it's not the only one.

The Dutch striker's move was hugely dramatic at the time, with plenty of fans turning on a former favourite. United will have considered the move a success after his goals brought an immediate league title but the following two years were less fruitful for player and club and he left for Fenerbahce in 2015.

‌



5. Emile Smith Rowe (£27.2m)

Academy graduate Smith Rowe made a fast start as a teenager but found himself overtaken in the pecking order during Mikel Arteta's tenure. He left for Fulham in 2024, with Mikel Merino brought in by Arteta just weeks later.

The three-cap England international has remained a solid presence in Fulham's midfield, featuring in 71 of 76 available league matches. However, he has not looked close to a Three Lions recall, nearly four years on from his most recent cap.

‌



4. Cesc Fabregas (£29.1m)

Your eyes don't deceive you. That's a 2011 sale in the top five - by way of comparison, Chelsea have sold 20 players for more money since then, give or take the margin of error for conversions between Euros and Pounds.

It was one of two big-money moves for Fabregas in his career, with the Spaniard also joining Chelsea in 2014 for a similar amount to the Barcelona deal after Arsenal opted against bringing him back. He won two Premier League titles with the Blues and has now made an impressive start to his managerial career with Como.

3. Alexis Sanchez (£29.1m)

You might not even want to count this one, given the fact that it came as part of an effective swap deal. We're leaving it in just to emphasise the task facing Berta as he looks to succeed where his predecessors struggled.

‌



Sanchez moved to United in 2018, with Henrikh Mkhitaryan joining Arsenal from the Red Devils. The Londoners came out of the deal a little better but neither club had huge success from the arrangement.

2. Nicolas Anelka (£30m)

Those tricky conversion fees mean reports vary for how much Anelka went for in Pounds. Even so, it says a lot that a sale from 1999 features on this list.

View 4 Images Anelka joined Real Madrid more than a quarter of a century ago (Image: Getty)

‌



Anelka was an example of Arsenal turning a huge profit on a player they signed for less than £1m from Paris Saint-Germain. He would go on to make more than 500 career league appearances across several countries and also played for France at the World Cup and European Championships.

1. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (£35m)

Arsenal's record sale remains the £35m they received when Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool in 2017. The England international became a Premier League and Champions League winner during his time at Anfield but was plagued by injury.

Despite spending six years as a Liverpool player, he made just 103 league appearances. He left for Besiktas on a free transfer in 2023 and is now at Celtic.

Sports.title: Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them
Sports.content:
Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them

Transfer sagas spanning years is a situation Liverpool know a thing or two about

View 5 Images Nabil Fekir's failed move to Liverpool was shrouded in controversy (Image: NurPhoto/PA Images)

Few things ignite the football world quite like a transfer saga, and Liverpool have certainly starred in their fair share over the years. There's been plenty of wins in the market for the Reds, such as their past acquisitions of Mohamed Salah and Sadio Mane, or besting Bayern Munich to the signing of Florian Wirtz last summer.

‌



High-stakes moves trigger an intense mix of fan hype and deadline-day anxiety, but the tension usually dissolves the second a player hits the pitch in red. Every so often, however, years of following a particular target and intense negotiations end in heartbreak.

‌



From controversial collapses of deals to players simply opting for another club, Mirror Football takes a look at five targets Liverpool failed to drag across the finish line - and why the deals fell apart.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Nabil Fekir

Arguably the most infamous collapsed transfer in recent Liverpool history, the breakdown of Nabil Fekir's switch to Anfield in 2018 sparked accusations of dishonesty and family drama. The Frenchman had undergone a medical ahead of his £53million transfer from Lyon and agreed personal terms before the Reds pulled out of the deal.

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole READ MORE :

The attacking midfielder had even posed for promotional photographs with the club, who insisted their decision to abandon the deal was down to a knee cartilage issue. Fekir dismissed the Reds' explanation as a lie and rejected claims from his then-agent, Jean-Pierre Bernes, who suggested that the Frenchman's brother-in-law tried to secure a cut from the transfer.

‌



"Lots of lies were told, and they affected me," Fekir told L'Equipe in 2019. "Especially those told about my family. It hurt them and me. Especially when you know that what's being told is false.

"What was said is not the truth. My knee is good - I had a quick medical check at Clairefontaine [the headquarters of France's national team] - my knee wasn't even mentioned. If my knee had been in such a bad state, would [then-Lyon chairman Jean-Michel Aulas] have made [a sufficient offer to keep the player]?"

Gareth Barry

View 5 Images Gareth Barry was wanted twice by Rafael Benitez (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Countdown to Kickoff: The Ultimate 26/27 Sky Sports Bundle This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £44 Sky Get the deal here Product Description Sky's Ultimate TV and Sky Sports bundle includes at least 215 live Premier League clashes across the 2026/27 season with more than 1,400 live games across the EFL and beyond, plus F1, golf and darts. Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Liverpool's pursuit of Gareth Barry began in the summer of 2008. A vital component of Aston Villa's midfield engine room, Rafael Benitez had identified the Englishman as the ideal replacement for Xabi Alonso, who had endured an injury-disrupted campaign throughout 2007/08.

Yet the Reds fell short of Villa's £18m valuation for their skipper, forcing Barry to remain at the Midlands club. Liverpool returned to the negotiating table twelve months on, with their persistent interest in the midfielder ultimately prompting Alonso to seal a switch to Real Madrid.

‌



It proved a double setback for Benitez as Barry chose Manchester City over Anfield. Reflecting on his decision to snub Liverpool, Barry told Birmingham Live's Claret and Blue podcast: "Something appealed to me more about Man City than Liverpool at the time. Liverpool had won the Champions League not so long ago and Man City hadn't won a trophy for many years, but I went with that route."

Arda Turan

View 5 Images Arda Turan was linked to the Reds during his time at Galatasaray and Atletico Madrid (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Arda Turan was repeatedly linked with a switch to Liverpool over a six-year period between 2009 and 2015. The speculation started during his stint at Galatasaray, but it was Atletico Madrid who secured his services in 2011.

‌



His impressive four-year spell in the Spanish capital, which featured their La Liga triumph in 2014, didn't halt talk of his possible arrival on Merseyside, according to AS. It was claimed the Turkish star grew up watching Liverpool and his father supported the club.

Despite his family's reported affection for the Reds, Turan never turned out for the club and instead moved to Barcelona in 2015, before hanging up his boots in 2022 with Galatasaray.

Simao Sabrosa

We're turning back the clock with Simao Sabrosa. A prominent figure in Portuguese football during the 2000s, the former forward came within touching distance of joining the Reds in the summer of 2005 before Benfica pulled out of the arrangement.

‌



A reported £10m deal had been struck between the two clubs, with Simao even leaving Portugal's training camp to undergo a medical. The 46-year-old opened up about the collapsed transfer in 2022, when speaking to Liverpoolfc.com.

He recounted: "At that time I'm in the national team, three or four days until the end [of the window]. I received a call at like five o'clock in the morning, 'You need to come, we go to Liverpool.'

View 5 Images Simao Sabrosa was inches away from becoming a Liverpool player (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

‌



"I go to [Luiz Felipe] Scolari and the director of the national team to give me permission to go out. When I go to the office of my agent, in that moment the president of Benfica called and said, 'We don't have a deal, you don't have permission to fly, so you need to stay.'

"It's strange because I thought it was done. But when the president went home, he called again and said, 'It's impossible to fly to Liverpool and get a new contract with Liverpool, so you need to stay. Because if you sign for Liverpool, Benfica fans will be angry [with me].' At that time I said, 'OK, I stay.'

"The office of my agent is near the airport and the agent gave me some impression, 'Let's go to the airport. When we arrive in Liverpool, maybe the president says yes.' I said, 'No, it's impossible to take the plane and fly to Liverpool.'

‌



"I was representing the national team and if I take this decision, I have a lot of problems with the national team, my club, so I decided to stay." His switch to Atletico Madrid in 2007 did little to silence ongoing speculation of a transfer to Anfield, but nothing advanced as close as it had a year prior.

Julian Draxler

The former Germany international is another footballer familiar to Liverpool supporters. The 32-year-old, who presently features for Qatari outfit Al-Ahli, emerged into the spotlight with boyhood side Schalke in 2011, which is when his enduring connections to Liverpool commenced.

Former Reds manager Brendan Rodgers reportedly made a personal trip to the Veltins-Arena to run the rule over Draxler during a Champions League clash against Basel. However, a deal never came to fruition as the attacking midfielder ultimately joined fellow Bundesliga outfit Wolfsburg in 2015.

‌



View 5 Images Julian Draxler opted to join Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Getty Images)

A switch to Paris Saint-Germain followed two years on, though not before Liverpool had once again registered their interest in the 2014 World Cup winner, this time under Jurgen Klopp. The German tactician was eager to bring compatriot Draxler to Merseyside, but the player chose a move to the French capital instead.

He has since admitted to pondering what might have unfolded had he chosen to test himself in the Premier League. "When I was still very young at Schalke and extended my contract, I could have gone to Arsenal," he told BILD, as quoted by Sport Witness.

Article continues below

"Honestly, I'd be interested to see what would have become of me if I had learned from Arsene Wenger so early. I've also wondered what would have happened if I hadn't gone from Wolfsburg to Paris, but to Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. I had that opportunity, too. Nevertheless, I'm happy. I'm at peace with my decisions."

"It did definitely open a lot of eyes, my last fight [against Smith], because of the fashion I did it in, it was a really dominant fight in my favour," McKenna told Sky Sports.

"To fight a former world champion in Liam Smith was a massive name to have on my record. A lot of people were predicting me to lose. So that was another bonus, once I beat him in the fashion I did, it opened a lot of eyes and really got my name out there.

"Going into that fight I was the underdog and not many people gave me a chance. But I knew that was my time to really show the world how good of a boxer I am. Not many people expected me to have that style but I've been saying it for years, of how good of a boxer I am.

"I want the biggest and best fights, I want to take on guys with undefeated records, or guys who are world champions and prove to myself I'm the best in the world. If I can't get the champions at 160lb, I'll take them on at 168lb, it doesn't matter to me. I'll take care of business on Saturday first."

Sports.title: Van Barneveld fined and suspended in latest Darts Regulation Authority case list
Sports.content:
Five-time world champion Raymond van Barneveld has been fined and suspended by the Darts Regulation Authority for inappropriate behaviour and offensive language.

The DRA, who are the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, have published an updated case list for the first time since 2022 listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Raymond van Barneveld talks us through his greatest game as he beat Phil Taylor in the final of the 2007 World Championship

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies handed four-month suspension

Image: Cameron Menzies repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby at the World Championship

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed, with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dom Taylor impressed on his Ally Pally debut in a first round win over Oskar Lukasiak at the World Championship with three 100+ checkouts.

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18, as well as £1,275 in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the Committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the Committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these Rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month Substance Abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

Sports.title: Massey-Ellis retires from officiating to take up new role with FA
Sports.content:
Assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis has retired from officiating and will take up a new role with the Football Association.

Massey-Ellis will become the FA's Senior Manager - Women Referees from September, where she will support and develop female officials across the country and help provide a pathway into the elite game.

The 40-year-old became only the second female assistant referee to officiate in the Premier League when she made her top-flight debut in 2010 and has since worked on more than 150 Premier League matches.

Her career also included five Women's FA Cup finals, while she became the first female assistant referee appointed to the Community Shield. In 2021, Massey-Ellis became the first woman involved in a men's FA Cup final when she served as an assistant VAR, before also working as an AVAR at the 2025 Carabao Cup final.

On the international stage, Massey-Ellis officiated at four Women's European Championships and two Women's World Cups, as well as the 2018 Women's Champions League final. In 2019, she became the first English woman to officiate a men's European fixture when she worked as an assistant referee in the Europa League.

To the young girl who simply loved refereeing, we did it. Thank you, football.

Massey-Ellis, who received an MBE for services to football, said: "Although I am stepping away from the touchline, I am not stepping away from football.

"If my journey has helped change perceptions, open doors or inspire even one young person to believe they belong in the game, then I will consider that one of my greatest achievements.

"As I prepare for one final walk onto the pitch, I leave with nothing but gratitude. It has been the greatest honour to serve the game I love and represent English officiating."

Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb described Massey-Ellis as a "powerhouse" whose impact on female officiating "will be felt for years to come".

"Sian has done us proud time and time again - domestically and on the international stage, breaking multiple barriers and setting the standard for those coming through in her footsteps," Webb added.

Sports.title: The Hundred permutations: Who needs what to qualify?
Sports.content:
We are into crunch time in the 2026 edition of The Hundred, with knockout spots up for grabs in the men's and women's competitions. But who will claim them, and who needs what?

The men's and women's sides that finish first in their respective tables after the eight group games secure direct qualification to the finals at Lord's on Sunday August 16.

The teams coming second and third will meet in the eliminator at The Kia Oval on Friday August 14, with the winners of those matches then also making the final.

Here is the state of play as the league phase enters its final stages...

How points are scored in The Hundred? Win = four points

Tie/no result = two points

Defeat = no points

Men's competition

The Hundred - Men's standings Team Played Wins Losses No result/Tie Points Net run-rate Rockets 6 5 1 0 20 +0.893 MI London 6 4 2 0 16 +0.448 Brave 6 4 2 0 16 -0.537 Super Giants 6 3 3 0 12 +0.495 SunRisers 5 3 2 0 12 +0.348 Brave 6 2 4 0 8 +0.022 Spirit (E) 6 1 5 0 4 −0.458 Phoenix 5 1 4 0 4 -1.298

Barring the already-eliminated London Spirit, it is still wide open in the men's competition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Curran appeared to clash with a few former England team-mates after hitting the match-winning runs for MI London that eliminated London Spirit

Trent Rockets moved one step closer towards qualification for the latter stages as they surged four points clear at the top of the table on 20 points with a fifth victory in six on Wednesday night.

Birmingham Phoenix are up against it, level with Spirit at the bottom of the table on four points but having played a game less.

They are still capable of getting to 16 points and giving themselves a chance of reaching the eliminator with three closing wins - the tally MI London and Welsh Fire in second and third, respectively, have accrued after six games.

It means, though, that Phoenix simply MUST win on Friday against SunRisers Leeds, or their tournament too will be ended early.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch as SunRisers Leeds hit the record highest total in The Hundred against London Spirit

SunRisers Leeds and Manchester Super Giants look to be the biggest threats to the top three, locked together on 12 points, albeit Super Giants have played a game more.

Things are looking pretty bleak, meanwhile, for Southern Brave, on eight points after six games. They will likely have to win out and have other results go their way to be in with a sniff of qualification.

What is net run-rate? This is used to separate teams on the same number of points during a league format, in the way that goal difference does in football.

Net run-rate in The Hundred is the average runs scored by a team over 100 balls in each game minus the average runs scored against them over 100 balls in each game.

Women's competition

The Hundred - Women's standings Team Played Wins Losses No result/Tie Points Net run-rate Rockets 6 5 1 0 20 +1.605 Brave 6 5 1 0 20 +0.399 Super Giants 6 3 2 1 14 +0.613 Fire 6 3 3 0 12 +0.345 SunRisers 5 2 3 0 8 +0.319 Spirit 6 1 4 1 6 −0.643 MI London 6 1 4 1 6 −1.231 Phoenix 5 1 3 1 6 −1.954

The top two in the women's competition are all but confirmed, with table-toppers Trent Rockets joined on 20 points by Southern Brave after six games.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leading run-scorer in the women's competition Sophia Dunkley hit a quickfire half-century for Trent Rockets in their Hundred win over Birmingham Phoenix

Only Manchester Super Giants, in third on 14 points, are capable of overhauling either team's tally, while Welsh Fire and SunRisers Leeds are able to match that 20-point total by winning out.

Fire are currently fourth on 12 points and SunRisers fifth on eight, but having played a game less.

They face off on Sunday, meaning they will take points off each other in some way or form, so the Monday meeting between Rockets and Brave will likely be a battle for top spot, the winner progressing straight through to the final and avoiding the eliminator.

MI London kept their tournament alive when finally registering their first win on Thursday night against capital-city rivals London Spirit, a result that sees the teams level on six points after six games.

It means both must now win their remaining two matches, and have other results go their way, to even be in with a sniff of qualification for the eliminator.

Birmingham Phoenix are in a similarly bleak position stuck on six points, albeit with three games remaining, allowing them a tiny bit more room to manoeuvre over the closing stages.

Sports.title: Gallagher ready to show what he can do under De Zerbi at Spurs
Sports.content:
Timing in sport often defines a career and for Conor Gallagher and Tottenham Hotspur, it probably could not have been worse.

He arrived at Spurs last January from Atletico Madrid for £35m and within weeks boss Thomas Frank had been replaced by Igor Tudor, who by Gallagher's own admission "wasn't having me" as a player, as the club battled relegation.

It was tough times at Spurs and Gallagher could not see a way out of the slump.

However, the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi as head coach began to change everything. Tottenham avoided relegation to the Championship and Gallagher played his part, although in an emotional interview on the final day he admitted he had not been able to show fans what he was really about.

Gallagher believes now is the time to really start his Spurs story.

"It's time to kick on to try and show the fans what I can do." he told Sky Sports. "I want to be at my best to help the club go to where we should be.

"I think every footballer has things going on and hard, tough times because it's just life. Everyone has problems and I'm just really happy that we came out of it and I ended the season well.

"Hopefully, this is only the start of my Spurs career."

Gallagher's praise for De Zerbi

Image: Gallagher struggled before Roberto De Zerbi's arrival at Spurs

It feels a very different Gallagher sitting in the sunshine a few days out from the start of a new season.

Much of that is down to De Zerbi, who joined Spurs in March.

Gallagher said: "With me, it was just a confidence thing mainly and slightly a physical thing, which you get from just playing more games. I wasn't really used to that at that time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player De Zerbi admitted he is not sure whether Richarlison or Cristian Romero will remain Tottenham players come the start of the season

"The manager gave me a bit of my confidence back and I started playing more consistent minutes on the pitch.

"A lot of credit to the manager, but for him, it's only the start also."

De Zerbi's demanding reputation and intensity are clear to see but Gallagher admits he was still a little daunted during their first meeting.

He added: "He was a bit scary, especially the first time meeting him, but after a while it's not like that.

Image: De Zerbi (R) and Gallagher attend a press conference in pre-season

"He's actually a really nice man, but you know you can't mess around. You've got to do the right things and train right and give 100 per cent.

"As a coach, he's one of those coaches that you want to do well for. He shows a lot of belief in his players. He instils that confidence in the players. He makes you want to do your best for him and work as hard as you can.

"He always said, if you listen to me and stick with me and believe me, then we'll be fine. And that was when we were in the situation we were last season. So, he had full belief in himself and he kind of needs everyone on board with him for it to work. And everyone is and does just by the way he is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp backs his former club to have a 'strong season' after behaving like a 'big club' in the transfer window

That belief is reflected in the way De Zerbi talks about Gallagher.

In Sydney, during pre-season, the Spurs boss said when Gallagher is at his best, it is like Tottenham have an extra player - a remarkable turnaround from a player who a few months ago was struggling for minutes.

Gallagher smiles. "It's nice. I always try and give my best whenever I'm on the pitch. I feel like it should be my prime kind of years. I've kind of been at a load of teams already and had amazing experiences and loved every club I played for at that time.

"So, now I just want to have a bigger role and try and lead, I suppose, by example, on and off the pitch."

'De Zerbi wants to dominate everything'

Image: Gallagher and Spurs' new signing Sandro Tonali in pre-season action

Tottenham have backed De Zerbi heavily this summer, getting much of their business done early.

Almost £200m has been spent on new players - all with Premier League experience - and the early arrivals have given Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson a chance to create some chemistry in the squad.

For De Zerbi, building relationships is as important as building a team, and Gallagher says he loves a bit of team bonding.

He said: "We've got a really good group of people and footballers. The gaffer loves it - a team dinner and a few drinks and a bonding night out."

It is all part of what De Zerbi's vision for the club is and, perhaps, I suggest to Gallagher, we got a glimpse of it in one of their pre-season games with Chelsea, which was pretty fiery.

Gallagher's tackle was committed on Dario Essugo, too committed thought some, and without a prompt he holds his head in his hands and laughs.

"That tackle was not as bad as what it looked, to be fair," he said. "I had no intention of hurting anyone."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pre-season friendly highlights between Chelsea and Tottenham. Credit: SpursPlay

He added: "De Zerbi wants to dominate everything. He wants to have the ball and control games. And that's what he wants.

"He wants us to obviously win every game, like any manager would. But he believes we can dominate any team we play against if we play the right way and with the right personality."

Where that can take Tottenham this season will be fascinating after two 17th-placed finishes.

What will also be interesting is to see what Gallagher does next. "It feels perfect here," he finishes.

Perhaps now really is his time at Spurs.

Sports.title: Gibbs' Lions deal makes him NFL's highest-paid running back ever
Sports.content:
Jahmyr Gibbs is set to become the highest-paid running back in NFL history having agreed to a new three-year deal worth up to $75.7m (£56.3m) with the Detroit Lions.

Gibbs' agents Athletes First announced the deal Thursday, hours after he took the field for the first time since the Lions' training camp started. His agents also noted the new contract includes $51.5m (£38.3m) guaranteed for the Pro Bowler.

Two days earlier, Atlanta briefly made Bijan Robinson the NFL's highest-paid running back in history.

Gibbs had been participating in meetings at camp, but Thursday was his first appearance on the field, an indication the Lions and his agents were close to a deal. Gibbs held his right arm high and gave a thumbs-up when asked if an agreement was close as he walked off the practice field.

Gibbs changed his jersey number from 26 to 0 ahead of the 2025 season and rushed for 1,223 yards and 13 touchdowns, and had 77 receptions for 616 yards and five scores.
