World.title: England striker Toney charged with London nightclub assault
World.content:
England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an incident at a London nightclub.

The Metropolitan Police said Friday that Toney, 30, was charged on Thursday July 31 with assault causing actual bodily harm.

The force said the charge relates to an assault which reportedly took place on December 6 last year at a nightclub in the Soho district of central London.

Toney, who plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

The Sun newspaper reported on December 8 that Toney — who was in the England squad that reached the World Cup semi-finals last month — had been arrested after an alleged headbutt.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

AFP

World.title: ADC spokesman resigns in Gombe, fuels APC defection speculation
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Publicity Secretary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Gombe State, Abdulrahman Buba Zaune, has resigned from the party, triggering speculation over his next political move ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

Zaune announced his resignation in a letter dated August 5, 2026, addressed to the Chairman of the ADC in Zaune Ward, Dukku Local Government Area of the state.

In the letter obtained by our correspondent on Thursday, the former state party spokesman expressed appreciation to the ADC for the opportunity to serve in various capacities at the local government, state and national levels.

“I sincerely appreciate the political party for the opportunity to serve in different capacities ranging from the Local Government, State and National levels respectively.

“I therefore wish the party well,” he wrote.

The resignation letter, however, did not disclose the reason for his decision or reveal his next political destination.

His exit has nevertheless sparked speculations within political circles that he may be considering joining the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The development came barely 24 hours after the APC governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr. Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna, visited Dukku Local Government Area, Zaune’s home constituency, as part of his political engagements.

The timing of Zaune’s resignation has further heightened interest as political parties intensify consultations and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

His resignation also follows the recent exit of ADC State Secretary, Ahmed Gana, who left the opposition party and later defected to the APC, declaring support for Gwamna’s governorship ambition.

Political observers believe Zaune’s departure could further affect the ADC’s structure in Gombe as political realignments continue ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: CAF Champions League: Rangers, Rivers Utd learn opponents
World.content:
CAF Champions League trophy

By Enitan Abdultawab

Rangers International and Rivers United have been drawn against their opponents for the first qualifying round of the 2026/27 CAF Champions League.

Rangers will face AS Sobemap of Benin Republic, while Rivers United have been drawn against Ivorian side San Pedro.

Rangers, who won the Nigeria Premier Football League title last season, will host AS Sobemap in the first leg at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne before travelling for the return fixture.

AS Sobemap are making their continental debut after winning their first-ever league title in Benin Republic last season.

Should Rangers progress, they will face the winner between ASN Nigelec of Niger Republic and Algerian giants MC Alger in the second qualifying round, with a place in the group stage at stake.

Rivers United, meanwhile, will begin their campaign away from home against San Pedro before hosting the Ivorian side in the return leg.

San Pedro secured their first league title in Ivory Coast last season and will be hoping to carry that form into their continental campaign.

If Rivers United advance, they will meet either Uganda’s Vipers or FC Nouadhibou of Mauritania in the next qualifying round for a place in the group stage.

The first-leg fixtures are scheduled for September 4 to 6, while the return legs will take place from September 11 to 13.

Meanwhile, Nigeria will also have two representatives in the CAF Confederation Cup.

Shooting Stars have been drawn against Tunisian club CS Sfaxien, while President Federation Cup winners El-Kanemi Warriors will face Guinea-Bissau’s União Desportiva Internacional de Bissau (UDIB).

Nigeria has not had multiple clubs feature in the CAF Champions League and Confederation Cup in the same season since the 2019/20 campaign, when Enyimba and Rangers represented the country.

The four Nigerian clubs will now begin preparations for their respective continental campaigns, with the first qualifying ties scheduled for September.

World.title: Media Experts Seek Stronger African Action Against South Africa’s Xenophobic Violence
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Veteran journalist and Editor-in-Chief of Newswatch, Ray Ekpu, Thursday, called on the Nigerian government to intensify diplomatic engagement with South Africa over recurring xenophobic attacks, insisting that Pretoria must enforce its laws, prosecute perpetrators and compensate victims.

He made the call at a Pan-African roundtable organised by League of Nigerian Columnists (LNC) in partnership with the Commonwealth Institute of Advanced and Professional Studies.

The dialogue themed, ‘From Mayibuye IAfrica to Abahambe! South Africa and Other African Countries: Reflections on the Trajectory of a Relationship’, was attended by scholars, diplomats, media professionals and policy analysts.

Ekpu, who chaired the occasion, emphasised the persistent attacks against foreign nationals in South Africa and criticised the government for what he described as its failure to decisively condemn the violence and ensure that law enforcement agencies protect immigrants.

According to him, while South Africa has laws to deal with criminal behaviour, authorities have failed to adequately enforce them.

“The South African government has not come out categorically to condemn what is going on, and the police appear to be looking the other way while these crimes are taking place. Those who violate the law should be dealt with according to the rule of law,” he stated.

Ekpu urged the Nigerian government to increase diplomatic pressure on Pretoria rather than resorting to retaliatory measures against South African-owned businesses operating in Nigeria.

He also opposed calls to target the more than 120 South African companies in Nigeria, arguing that such action would hurt Nigerians more than South Africans because the majority of employees in those firms are Nigerians.

“I do not believe in an eye-for-an-eye approach. If we go that route, Africa will only destroy itself. We should pursue coexistence and continue building Pan-Africanism,” he said.

The media icon stressed that Africa already faces numerous challenges, including economic hardship, migration, climate change and political instability, adding that the continent cannot afford further divisions.

On the plight of Nigerians displaced by xenophobic attacks, Ekpu called on the South African government to compensate victims for their losses, while urging the Nigerian government to provide support for those returning home to rebuild their lives.

“The South African government should pay compensation, while our own government should help those who have returned to resettle and start life again,” he said.

Ekpu attributed the continued migration of many Nigerians to the country’s difficult economic conditions, noting that poor wages and limited opportunities push citizens to seek greener pastures abroad, where they often face exploitation and discrimination.

He maintained that improving the domestic economy would reduce the pressure on Nigerians to emigrate.

Speaking with journalists, Jean Monnet Professor of Strategy and Development, Anthony Kila, called for coordinated diplomatic and strategic action by African governments and the African Union (AU) to bring an end to recurring xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

He warned that failure to act could have grave economic and social consequences for the country and the continent.

The persistent attacks on foreign nationals, he stated, required more than periodic condemnations, adding that African leaders must adopt concrete measures to compel South African authorities to address the crisis.

According to him, South Africa should invest in reorienting its citizens through what he described as soft diplomacy, while the AU and individual African governments should engage Pretoria more firmly to ensure that xenophobic violence is no longer tolerated.

“I think South Africans in the diaspora, South African businesses operating internationally and the government need to invest in reorientation. They need to explain to people why they should not behave in such a barbaric manner,” he said.

Kila, who is also a Political Economist, suggested that African countries could consider diplomatic measures, including boycotting selected South African events, while urging influential South African public figures to speak out more forcefully against xenophobia.

He warned that the continued targeting of other Africans would eventually deepen divisions within South Africa itself.

“Today it is South Africans against other Africans. Tomorrow it could become Zulu against non-Zulu. If this trend continues, they will eventually turn on themselves,” he said.

He also urged African governments to tackle the underlying economic conditions that force many of their citizens to migrate in search of better opportunities.

“Governments should ask themselves why their citizens are so desperate to leave their countries to seek better lives elsewhere, only to become vulnerable to exploitation and attacks,” he said.

In his remarks, veteran journalist and Media Consultant, Martins Oloja, called on Nigerian leaders to improve governance, strengthen the economy and invest in quality education as a long-term solution to the growing migration of Nigerians and recurring xenophobic attacks against Africans in South Africa.

He stated that African governments should focus on addressing the conditions that force citizens to leave their countries in search of better opportunities, rather than merely condemning attacks whenever they occur.

According to him, poverty, weak governance and poor educational outcomes have continued to drive migration across the continent, making many Africans vulnerable to discrimination and violence abroad.

“They should improve conditions at home, improve the quality of education. Quality leads to industrialisation. It is quality that leads to innovation and helps fight poverty, which is why people are leaving their countries,” he said.

Oloja described the xenophobic attacks in South Africa as a reflection of broader governance failures across Africa, blaming not only the South African government but also continental institutions, including the AU and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), for failing to provide effective leadership.

He also criticised South African authorities for allowing citizens to take the law into their own hands by attacking immigrants and destroying property, insisting that the country’s leadership must act decisively to restore order and protect all residents.

Oloja also challenged African leaders to place greater emphasis on governance, economic development and regional integration instead of concentrating excessively on politics.

He expressed concern over the slow pace of African integration, citing poor transportation links across West Africa compared to Europe, where citizens can move seamlessly by road, rail or air.

“The African Union and ECOWAS should be playing stronger roles in addressing these challenges,” he said, adding that African governments must create opportunities that discourage the mass migration of young people.

He argued that countries should focus on building globally competitive businesses capable of expanding across the continent, pointing to South Africa’s success in developing multinational companies and world-class universities.

A Tanzanian Economist and Development expert, Prof. Bravious Felix Kahyoza, urged South Africa to reinforce its commitment to Pan-Africanism by protecting migrants, promoting social inclusion and educating its citizens on the historical role African countries played in the struggle against apartheid.

He stated that many African migrants, including Nigerians in South Africa, were driven by economic hardship rather than criminal intent, adding that: “Governments across the continent must create better economic opportunities to reduce irregular migration.”

He noted that many migrants were vulnerable because they were searching for improved livelihoods and often took dangerous risks in pursuit of better opportunities abroad.

“Across Africa, particularly within the continent, we need to do better so that our citizens can feel secure and have opportunities at home,” he said. “Reducing vulnerability will also reduce the pressure for people to migrate under difficult circumstances.”

While acknowledging that migrants must respect the laws of their host countries, Kahyoza said it was equally important for South Africa to improve the way it manages migration and treatment of foreign nationals.

He called on South African authorities to sensitise citizens on the importance of Pan-African solidarity, reminding them that many African nations stood firmly behind the country’s liberation struggle.

World.title: Jessica Oji Wins Historic World U20 Athletics Championships Shot Put Gold
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

Nineteen-year-old Jessica Oji early hours of Friday became the first Nigerian to win a world title in a field event at the World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon, United States.

Oji heaved a massive 18.08 metres to take the women’s shot put event gold, leaving the silver medal for Belsy Jenniffer Quiñonez (17.90m) of Ecuador while Emily Scherf (17.23m) of Germany settled for the bronze.

The feat of Oji is coming up barely one week after winning a silver medal at her first competition in Nigeria’s colours at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland.

She didn’t leave anyone in doubt about her capacity to take the gold medal at the World U20. Oji kicked off her campaign with 18.05m, before she improved to her winning throw of 18.08m. Her third effort was 17.95m, before another 18.07m . All her efforts were good enough for the gold as Quiñonez of Ecuador’s best for the silver was 17.90m.

Interestingly, Oji just last February completed her switch of allegiance from the United States of America to Nigeria.

She celebrated her 19th birthday at Team Nigeria’s training camp in Aberdeen on June 23 while preparing for the Commonwealth Games.

Oji’s best effort at Glasgow 2026 was 17.87m that earned her the silver medal. Now, she has stepped into the 18.00m mark even as a junior athlete, giving Nigeria the hope having a shot put star in the ranks of world’s best throwers .

In a chat with THISDAY at the Commonwealth Games, Oji, said that competing for Nigeria gives her joy. “If I don’t compete for Nigeria where else? I love the vibes, the atmosphere around the Nigerian camp and all around me here in Glasgow. I will go to the World U20 Championships to give my best,” Oji stressed in the interview at the Team Nigeria Maldron Hotel camp in the Scottish capital city.

Until Oji’s achievement early hours of Friday, Nigeria’s previous efforts at the U20 Championships were Esther Aghatise’s silver medal in the women’s long jump in 2002 and Chinecherem Nnamdi’s bronze medal in the men’s javelin event in 2021.

Elsewhere at the Championships, Team Nigeria continued its impressive showing in Eugene with a record-breaking performance in the mixed 4x100m relay, while Jecinta Lawrence, Faith Ezechukwu and Precious Opinion also secured progression in their respective events.

The mixed 4x100m quartet of Tejiri Godwin, Rosemary Nwankwo, Perfect Faye and Miracle Ezechukwu produced one of Nigeria’s standout performances so far, clocking 41.91 seconds to finish second in their heat and qualify for the final.

Nigeria entered the final exchange behind the leading teams, but Ezechukwu produced a sensational anchor leg, ghosting past Germany and almost catching the United States before the finish line.

Ezechukwu recorded a stunning 10.05-second anchor split as Nigeria crossed the line in 41.91 seconds, a Nigerian U20 record and the fastest U20 time ever recorded by an African team in the event.

The performance puts Nigeria firmly in the medal conversation heading into the final, with the quartet now looking to build on an impressive opening-round performance and challenge the world’s leading teams for a place on the podium.

There was further progress for Nigeria in the women’s 400m as Jecinta Lawrence and Faith Ezechukwu both advanced to the semifinals.

Lawrence battled all the way to the finish in her heat, clocking 53.97 seconds in a dead heat for third place with Eni Kuske, with both athletes credited with the same time.

Faith Ezechukwu followed with another composed performance, finishing third in her heat in 54.38 seconds to secure automatic qualification for the semifinals.

Nigeria also celebrated an impressive breakthrough in the men’s triple jump as Precious Opinion produced a new personal best of 16.02m in the qualification round.

World.title: ASUSS Raises Concerns over Attacks on Schools, Urges Govt to take Proactive Measures
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja

The Academic Staff Union of Secondary Schools(ASUSS), Kogi State chapter, has expressed serious concern over the persistent attacks on schools and educational communities in the country and the state in particular.

This was contained in a communique issued by the Executive Council(EC) of the ASUSS and copy of which was made available to journalists in Lokoja yesterday, lamenting that that schools are centres of learning and should never become targets of criminal activities.

The council therefore, called on government and all security agencies to strengthen security around schools through proactive intelligence.

The council, however, commended the Kogi State Government under the leadership of the Governor Usman Ododo, for its sustained efforts in improving security across the state and for maintaining a cordial relationship with the workforce.

“We acknowledge the government’s commitment to industrial harmony and appreciate the steps taken to promote the welfare of workers.

“The council also passionately appeals to the Kogi State Government to restore the payment of the 27.5 per cent Teachers’ Special Allowance (TSA) to secondary school teachers. This allowance was a product of a duly negotiated Collective Bargaining Agreement between ASUSS and the Government and served as recognition of the peculiar demands of the teaching profession.

‘Its restoration will greatly improve teachers’ morale and further demonstrate Government’s commitment to quality education.

“On healthcare, the council commended the Government for introducing the Kogi State Health Insurance Scheme, which has the capacity to improve access to quality healthcare for workers and their families.

“We, however, observe that some of our members have not yet enrolled in the scheme. We therefore urge all secondary school teachers to complete their enrolment without delay so they can enjoy its numerous benefits.

“The council further expresses concern over the piecemeal payment of gratuities to retired workers in the state. While we appreciate government’s efforts to settle outstanding liabilities, we respectfully appeal that gratuities be paid in more reasonable and substantial batches to enable our retired colleagues enjoy the rewards of their many years of dedicated service.

“Another major concern is the acute shortage of teachers in our public secondary schools. The shortage has placed enormous pressure on the available teachers and is affecting the quality of teaching and learning. We therefore renew our appeal to Government to urgently recruit qualified teachers to fill existing vacancies across the state.

“The council equally calls on government to establish a motorcycle loan scheme for secondary school teachers, especially those serving in rural communities where transportation remains a major challenge. Such a programme will improve teachers’ mobility, enhance punctuality, and boost productivity,” the Communique stressed.

“Despite these challenges, the council commends all teachers for their resilience, professionalism, and commitment to duty under difficult economic and working conditions. We encourage our members to remain dedicated, maintain the highest standards of discipline and professionalism, and continue to discharge their responsibilities with diligence in the overall interest of our students and the state.

“Finally, ASUSS wishes to reassure the Kogi State Government of our continued support and readiness to collaborate in advancing the development of secondary education. We remain committed to constructive engagement, mutual respect, and dialogue as the best means of addressing issues affecting teachers and the education sector.”

World.title: NAFDAC Flags Unregistered Menopause Supplement, Warns of Potential Health Risks
World.content:
Ayodeji Ake

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has issued a nationwide public alert over the sale and distribution of an unregistered menopause supplement, Menofix Capsules, warning Nigerians not to purchase or use the product as it is being removed from the market.

The agency said the product, marketed by PureEve as a hormone-free herbal and multivitamin supplement for women experiencing perimenopause and menopause, is not registered with NAFDAC despite being widely advertised and sold through online platforms and retail outlets across the country.

NAFDAC explained that the alert followed a complaint concerning the sale of the product and reports of possible liver-related adverse effects associated with some of its ingredients.

Following investigations, the agency confirmed that Menofix Capsules has never been registered by NAFDAC and is therefore not authorised for sale, distribution or use in Nigeria.

The regulator also cautioned consumers not to confuse the unregistered product with two legitimately approved products bearing similar names — Menofix Herbal Capsule (NAFDAC Registration No. A7-103321L) and Menofix Powder, both of which are duly registered with the agency.

NAFDAC said it has directed all its zonal directors and state coordinators to step up surveillance and immediately remove the unregistered product from circulation wherever it is found.

The agency urged distributors, retailers, healthcare providers and members of the public to remain vigilant and avoid stocking, selling or consuming the product. It also advised anyone in possession of Menofix Capsules to discontinue its use and submit any remaining stock to the nearest NAFDAC office.

Consumers who have used the product and experienced any adverse reactions were encouraged to seek immediate medical attention and report such incidents through NAFDAC’s official pharmacovigilance reporting channels.

The latest alert forms part of NAFDAC’s ongoing campaign to eliminate unregistered and potentially harmful medicines from the Nigerian market and safeguard public health.

World.title: SWIS Africa Launches Innovation Hub to Boost Women Participation in STEM
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Shaping African Women in STEM (SWIS Africa) has launched the SWIS Hub, a year-long digital innovation and mentorship initiative aimed at bridging the gender gap in science, technology, engineering and mathematics across Nigeria.

The organisation said the project would kick off with its first Pop-Up Innovation Lab in Lagos on Friday and Saturday, August 7 and 8, 2026, where young women would receive hands-on training in artificial intelligence and data science.

According to SWIS Africa, the programme is designed to equip participants with practical digital skills while connecting them with mentors, scholarships and career opportunities in STEM.

The project is funded through the AU-EU Youth Action Lab Innovation Grant, co-funded by the European Union and the African Union and managed by Oxfam Novib. The organisation said it was among the youth-led organisations selected across Africa and Europe to receive grants of between €30,000 and €40,000.

SWIS Africa was founded by Nigerian academics Samuel Ogunsola and Abosede Salami to address challenges limiting women’s participation in STEM, including poor access to mentorship, career information, professional networks and role models.

The organisation said the SWIS Hub would feature a digital platform, expected to go live this month, offering over 30 expert videos on STEM careers and skills, a searchable database of scholarships, fellowships and internships, educational resources, and networking opportunities for young women.

It added that four innovation labs would be organised across Nigeria during the project year, focusing on artificial intelligence, data science, science communication, digital tools and prototyping, before ending with an innovation showcase where participants would present solutions to STEM professionals.

The initiative will also include a six-month Media Fellowship to train 20 young women in science communication through monthly masterclasses and mentorship, while 10 STEM Circles will be established across the country to promote peer learning and collaboration.

Speaking on the launch, the Executive Director of SWIS Africa, Samuel Ogunsola, said the organisation remained committed to transforming the lives of young African women through access to STEM education and opportunities.

He said, “People sometimes look at plans like these and forget the significance and impact. We do not. Every lab, every mentorship session, every scholarship a young woman finds through the Hub is a life touched. We are changing lives and helping women in STEM get better, one young woman at a time.”

Ogunsola added that the project, which runs from May 2026 to April 2027, is expected to directly impact more than 500 young women through its training, mentorship and digital learning programmes.

World.title: Aina Bridges Music, Theatre, Healthcare in a Growing Creative Career
World.content:
Nigerian creative professional Ayobami Aina, popularly known as Ayo, is steadily establishing himself as a versatile force in music and theatre, building a career that seamlessly blends artistic expression with public service in the United Kingdom.

With a journey that began in church, where he discovered his passion for acting, singing and choreography, Ayo has evolved into a multidisciplinary creative whose work spans stage performance, music production, theatre management and technical production.

Over the years, he has remained committed to developing his craft, embracing opportunities that have positioned him within both the Nigerian and British creative landscapes.

His first major step into the music industry came in 2012 with the release of his debut song alongside a group of friends.

While studying at the University of Lagos, he continued to refine his artistic abilities, combining his academic pursuits with active participation in theatre productions and live performances that laid the foundation for his professional career.

Today, Ayo’s theatre résumé includes more than 15 productions in diverse capacities, including actor, director, stage manager, assistant stage manager and props manager.

His broad experience reflects an understanding of theatre that extends beyond performance to encompass the technical and managerial disciplines that sustain successful productions.

His dedication has earned him opportunities to collaborate with respected theatre practitioners such as Anne Neville, Alex Marker and Daniel Martin.

In music, he has also worked with internationally recognised British producer Anthony Adams, while maintaining creative partnerships with Nigerian producers Paul Emmanuel and IFE MOJ, acclaimed sound engineer SoundMindPro, and artists including Sydney, Timilehin Idowu and Paul Oluwapelumi.

Ayo is currently a member of Questors Theatre in the United Kingdom, where he has contributed to productions including Labour of Love, Everlasting Cake and The Curious Incident of the Cat in the Playhouse.

Across these productions, he has served as a cast member, assistant stage manager and band member, demonstrating the versatility that has become a defining feature of his career.

His responsibilities within the theatre continue to expand. He is scheduled to join the production teams for The Lover and the Slight Ache and Romeo and Juliet, where he will contribute to set design, further broadening his experience across different aspects of theatrical production.

A significant milestone came on July 19, 2026, when he served as Stage Manager for the musical theatre production Worship in Chaos.

The role required overseeing rehearsals, coordinating backstage operations and managing the technical execution of the production, underscoring his growing leadership within the theatre community.

Alongside his theatre work, Ayo has continued to build an impressive music catalogue. Since his debut release, he has released seven songs, comprising four singles and an extended play (EP) launched in December 2025.

His eighth single is scheduled for release in August 2026, while another collaboration with Anthony Adams is already in development.

His music has continued to gain international traction, attracting listeners in more than 14 countries on Spotify, with London emerging as one of his strongest streaming markets.

He has also performed at events across London, Grimsby and other parts of the United Kingdom, steadily expanding his audience through live performances.

Beyond the creative industry, Ayo serves as an Emergency Medical Advisor with the South East Coast Ambulance Service (SECAMB), balancing the demands of emergency healthcare with an active career in music and theatre.

His ability to excel in both fields reflects a disciplined approach to professional growth and service.

For Ayo, success has been defined less by rapid recognition than by consistency and continuous improvement.

Each production, recording and collaboration has contributed to a career built on versatility, professionalism and a commitment to excellence.

As he prepares for new music releases, theatre productions and international collaborations, Ayo continues to strengthen his profile as one of a new generation of Nigerian creatives making their mark beyond the country’s borders.

His story is one of purposeful growth, demonstrating how talent, discipline and resilience can create opportunities across multiple creative and professional landscapes.

World.title: Kebbi Governor Meets Security Chiefs To Review State Security Architecture
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

Kebbi State Governor, Dr. Nasir Idris, has convened another emergency security meeting as part of renewed efforts to contain emerging security challenges in some parts of the state.

The meeting, held in Birnin Kebbi, brought together heads of security agencies and key government officials to review the current security situation and strengthen the state’s security architecture.

Briefing journalists after the closed-door session, the Commissioner for Home Affairs and Internal Security, Hon. Haliru Wasagu, said the engagement was necessitated by the need to protect lives and property across the state.

According to Wasagu, deliberations focused on assessing existing strategies, identifying gaps, and fine-tuning operational responses to ensure a more coordinated approach to emerging threats.

He stated that Governor Idris directed security agencies to intensify patrols, surveillance, and intelligence gathering in flashpoints identified during the review.

The Commissioner stressed that the governor remains unwavering in his commitment to safeguarding residents and creating an enabling environment for economic activities to thrive.

“Our Governor is fully committed to flushing out criminal elements and dismantling their hideouts. Anyone found engaging in criminal activities will face the full weight of the law,” Wasagu quoted the governor as saying.

He added that the administration has continued to invest in logistics, mobility, and welfare for security personnel to enhance their effectiveness on the ground.

Wasagu also appealed to residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could aid in the identification, apprehension, and prosecution of criminal elements.

He emphasized that public vigilance and collaboration with security operatives remain critical to winning the fight against crime and maintaining peace in communities.

The Commissioner further commended the dedication, professionalism, and sacrifices of security agencies for their sustained efforts in ensuring peace, stability, and public safety across Kebbi State.

World.title: Alleged Off-budget Expenditure: Lawmakers Demand Emergency Reconvening of N’Assembly
World.content:
•Seek independent forensic audit of all reported off-budget expenditure

•Frown on under-implementation of the 2024, 2025, 2026 Appropriation Acts

•Lament constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Alteration Bill

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

A group of bi-partisan lawmakers in the House of Representatives under the aegis of Save Nigeria Group has called upon the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, to reconvene both Chambers immediately for an emergency session.

The emergency session, the lawmakers said, must address the issue of under-implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 Appropriation Acts; the constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill; and allegations of off-budget expenditure.

Other issues they want the parliament to address as a matter of urgency included: non-release of capital funds to security agencies; the deteriorating security situation; and measures required to restore public confidence in the rule of law and democratic governance.

The concerned lawmakers stated this in a statement issued Friday and jointly signed by Hon. Awaji-Inombek Abiante (NDC, Rivers); Hon. Abubakar Kusada, (APC, Katsina) and Hon. Mansur Jega (ADC, Kebbi) on behalf of the group.

The lawmakers clarified that they are neither an opposition platform nor an instrument of any political interest, rather they are legislators increasingly alarmed by the direction of Nigeria’s democracy and the growing tendency of public institutions to subordinate the Constitution.

The lawmakers lamented that Nigeria’s democracy is nosediving, adding that silence in the face of repeated constitutional violations and institutional failures could no longer be justified.

They pointed out that the country is confronting an alarming disregard for the rule of law, chronic budget under-implementation, allegations of off-budget expenditure, worsening economic hardship and an unacceptable security situation.

The concerned lawmakers emphasised that democracy cannot survive where constitutional procedures are treated as inconveniences and legal safeguards are replaced by political improvisation.

They expressed concern over the emerging pattern in which constitutionally prescribed procedures are treated as optional.

The lawmakers recalled that during the approval of the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State in March 2025, the National Assembly relied on voice votes despite the requirement under section 305(6) of the Constitution that the proclamation must be supported by a two-thirds majority of all members of each Chamber.

They said more recently, serious constitutional and procedural questions arose from the purported passage of the Executive State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill by the House of Representatives on 23 July 2026.

The lawmakers stated: “The Speaker announced that 311 members had voted in support of the Bill, thereby exceeding the constitutional threshold of 240 affirmative votes.

“However, some of us were physically present throughout the proceedings and can state categorically that at no time that day were as many as 240 members in the Chamber, particularly when the Bill was considered.

“The figure announced by the Speaker could only have been reached by including votes transmitted through WhatsApp by members who were absent from the Chamber at the material time.”

The lawmakers stressed that Section 9(2) of the Constitution requires the affirmative votes of not less than two-thirds of all members of each Chamber before the Constitution can be altered.

According to them, The mere announcement of figures by the Speaker cannot substitute for strict constitutional compliance.

They added: “The Constitution cannot be altered by presumption, improvisation or undisclosed voting arrangements.

“Democracy is endangered when a state of emergency can be approved through an unverifiable voice vote and the Constitution can purportedly be altered through WhatsApp messages.

“State Police may be desirable, but a desirable reform must still be established through a lawful process.”

The lawmakers further lamented that throughout the 2024, 2025 and 2026 fiscal cycles, Nigeria has experienced repeated budget extensions, rollovers and severe delays in capital implementation.

They said in 2025, the federal government indicated that only approximately 30 per cent of the 2025 capital budget would be funded, while about 70 per cent would be carried forward into 2026.

The lawmakers pointed out that it is no longer an occasional administrative delay, but a recurring breakdown of fiscal governance.

They further recalled that Senate Chief Whip, Mohammed Monguno, publicly described the failure to implement an Appropriation Act as a breach of the law capable of amounting to an “impeachable offence.”

They noted: “We agree with Senator Monguno that the deliberate or persistent refusal to implement duly enacted Appropriation Acts raises grave constitutional questions.

“Repeated rollovers weaken parliamentary oversight, confuse fiscal accountability and make it almost impossible for Nigerians to determine which projects belong to which financial year.”

To this end, the concerned lawmakers therefore demanded comprehensive budget implementation reports for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 fiscal years; full disclosure of capital releases made to every ministry, department and agency.

They further demanded reconciliation of revenues collected against expenditure authorised by the National Assembly; an explanation for the failure to release duly appropriated capital funds; and a joint parliamentary investigation into chronic budget under-implementation.

They also called for appropriate constitutional action where deliberate or unjustifiable non implementation is established.

The lawmakers said that the Appropriation Act is law, and the federal government cannot choose which laws to obey.

While decrying reports of unrecorded public expenditure, the lawmakers maintained that allegations of misappropriation must be established through competent investigation and due process.

Nevertheless, they were of the opinion that available reports provide sufficient grounds for immediate legislative scrutiny and forensic auditing.

The lawmakers also recalled that in July 2026, the International Monetary Fund reportedly stated that public expenditure equivalent to approximately two per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product had not been recorded in recent official budgets, an amount estimated at approximately ₦8.83 trillion.

The lawmakers emphasised that the reported unrecorded expenditure was said to have contributed to a discrepancy between Nigeria’s declared fiscal deficit and its actual financing requirements.

This matter, they insisted, cannot be dismissed through public relations or general denials by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

They noted: “Public funds cannot lawfully be spent outside duly enacted Appropriation Acts, concealed under opaque accounting classifications or omitted from fiscal information presented to the National Assembly and the Nigerian people.

“This administration cannot demand sacrifice from Nigerians while public expenditure remains opaque. Every naira spent by the Government belongs to the Nigerian people.

“Those entrusted with public funds must account for how the money was appropriated, released, expended and utilised.

“Budgetary opacity is not merely an accounting problem. It is a threat to constitutional government, public trust and Nigeria’s economic survival. We call for an independent forensic audit of all reported off-budget expenditure.”

On security, the lawmakers said while the protection of lives and property is the primary responsibility of government, Nigerians continue to be killed, kidnapped and displaced by terrorists, bandits, criminal gangs and other violent groups.

The lawmakers expressed worry by Monguno’s further disclosure that some security agencies had received no capital releases despite the worsening security situation.

They said reports indicated that approximately ₦20.27 billion, representing nearly the entire budgetary provision for the Presidential Air Fleet, was released, while only a small fraction of the Nigerian Army’s allocation for security equipment was made available during the period under review.

“The question is not whether the Presidential Air Fleet should be maintained. The question is why the comfort and mobility of public officials should receive more predictable funding than the equipment, logistics, operational vehicles, aircraft maintenance and protective resources required by personnel confronting terrorists and bandits,” they posited.

Against this background, the lawmakers called for the immediate release of duly appropriated capital funds to the Armed Forces, the Nigeria Police Force, intelligence institutions and other security agencies.

The lawmakers commended the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria for speaking candidly about insecurity, economic hardship, democratic decline and concerns about emerging one-party dominance.

They added that the Bishops have demonstrated that patriotism sometimes requires telling those in authority uncomfortable truths.

They also commended the Supreme Council for Shari’ah in Nigeria for urging caution, wider consultation and national consensus before the establishment of State Police.

The lawmakers noted that Nigeria’s present circumstances do not permit the legislature to remain away from plenary while urgent constitutional, fiscal, economic and security questions remain unresolved.

They stated: “We call upon the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives to reconvene both Chambers immediately for an emergency session.

“The session must address: chronic under-implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets; the constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill; allegations of off-budget expenditure; non-release of capital funds to security agencies; the deteriorating security situation; and measures required to restore public confidence in the rule of law and democratic governance.”

They said the National Assembly is not merely an institution for passing Executive Bills and approving requests from the Presidency, but an independent arm of government constitutionally empowered to represent the people, defend the Constitution, appropriate public funds, conduct oversight and hold the Executive accountable.

The lawmakers stated categorically that while they are not opposed to State Police, economic reform or necessary public expenditure, they are however opposed to unconstitutional procedures, legislative shortcuts, unimplemented budgets, opaque expenditure and the continuing failure to protect the Nigerian people.

World.title: Does snow actually matter for Cape Town’s dams?
World.content:
Snow looks dramatic on the mountains above Cape Town, but rain does most of the real work filling the dams: Image Pexels

With fresh snowfall forecast for parts of the Western Cape this weekend, many Capetonians are asking the same question: Does snow on the mountains help fill the city’s dams?

The short answer is yes – but only a little.

While snow eventually melts and contributes some runoff, it’s rainfall rather than snowfall that does the heavy lifting when it comes to replenishing Cape Town’s water supply.



Rain is the real source of Cape Town’s water

Cape Town’s drinking water comes from six major dams that make up the Western Cape Water Supply System, with Theewaterskloof Dam accounting for more than half of the network’s total storage capacity.

As of Thursday, 6 August, the combined dam system was sitting at 77.7% full – a healthy level for this stage of the winter rainfall season.

The water entering these dams comes overwhelmingly from sustained rainfall over the surrounding mountain catchments, rather than melting snow.

Although parts of the Western Cape experienced an early snowfall this winter, snow alone has little impact on overall dam levels.

Snow helps, but rainfall does the heavy lifting

Snow that settles on the high peaks around Villiersdorp, Franschhoek and other mountain catchments eventually melts and flows into rivers feeding the dams.

However, that contribution is relatively small compared with prolonged winter rain.



In contrast, widespread rainfall across the catchment areas can dramatically boost storage levels.

During one particularly wet spell in May, Cape Town’s dam system recorded an increase of around 20 percentage points in just a single week – far more than any snowfall event has contributed this year.

Good news for water security

While snow remains one of winter’s most spectacular sights in the Western Cape, hydrologists generally regard it as a bonus rather than a major source of water.

For residents hoping this weekend’s snow will significantly boost dam levels, the reality is that the accompanying rain is far more important.

The snowfall may add a small amount of runoff once it melts, but it’s the steady winter rainfall across the mountain catchments that ultimately keeps Cape Town’s taps flowing.

You can track the current combined dam level here, and see how this weekend’s system is expected to unfold.

Did you know snow played such a small part in Cape Town’s water supply?

World.title: ‘Basadi in Music Awards’ to honour Bonang Matheba with Trailblazer Award
World.content:
South African media personality and businesswoman Bonang Matheba is on track to receive the Trailblazer Award at the Basadi in Music Awards.

The award ceremony is scheduled for 8 August at the Joburg Theatre.

Matheba has been in the media industry for over 23 years, having gotten her start on Manhattan’s Fantasy Challenge at age 15.



Bonang Matheba. Image via Instagram/@basadiinmusicawards_sa

In addition to her stints in radio, namely YFM and Metro FM, she has extensive experience on television. She has been a presenter on Tswelopele Productions’ Top Billing and has left her mark on many major events, including the Miss South Africa pageant, the MTV EMAs, and Global Citizen.

International doors are wide open for 38-year-old Matheba, especially after she won major praise for her hosting skills at Miss Cosmo 2025 Grand Finale & Beauty Music Festival in Vietnam.

Matheba’s fashion footprint has also made her a darling, not only to her fans but to designers as well. She is known for her opulent gowns and daring style.

“Some people succeed within an industry. Bonang Matheba transformed it. She showed an entire generation of African women that it is possible to dream without limits, occupy spaces once thought unattainable and build a globally respected brand while remaining unapologetically African,” said Basadi in Music Awards (BIMAs) founder and CEO Hloni Modise Matau.

“The Trailblazer Award is reserved for individuals whose impact changes the course of an industry. Bonang has done exactly that. She has inspired women to own their voices, recognise their value and understand that success is something you intentionally create,” she added, according to Music in Africa.



Bonang Matheba, the business mogul

Matheba has not only perfected her craft in media, but is making strides in business too.

Her most notable business is House of BNG, her flagship luxury beverage brand, with its Brut and Brut Rosé Méthode Cap Classiques (MCCs), and Prestige Reserve MCC.

BNG Beauty is an extension of the House of BNG.

She owns her own management and production company, Bonang Matheba Entertainment, which handles her media, television, and global production work.

World.title: Confirmed: Mbekezeli Mbokazi flying to Europe for surgery
World.content:
The setback has ended Mbokazi’s MLS season, delayed a potential European transfer and ruled him out of Bafana Bafana’s upcoming 2027 AFCON qualifiers.

Clubs in Italy were among those monitoring the Chicago Fire defender, but the transfer cannot happen until he fully recovers.

MBEKEZELI MBOKAZI TO UNDERGO SURGERY

Speaking exclusively to SABC Sport‘s Mazola Molefe, Basia Michaels of QT Sport confirmed that the injury has halted all transfer plans.



“Any transfer for Mbokazi would require him to successfully complete a medical, and the current situation makes that impossible because of the severity of his injury. Unfortunately, any plans to transfer the player will have to be put on hold,” said Michaels.

She also confirmed that Mbokazi will head to Finland for surgery.

“We’ve been working over the past week to determine the best course of action for his recovery. He will now head to Finland to work with a specialist and have the operation.

“There remains interest in his services, but at the moment that’s something we simply cannot explore because of the current setback,” she added.

Despite the injury, European clubs remain interested in the defender. However, any move must wait until he returns to full fitness.

BAFANA BAFANA SUFFER MAJOR BLOW

The injury is also a major setback for Bafana Bafana. Mbokazi is expected to miss South Africa’s opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches in September, October and November.



His absence leaves the national team’s incoming head coach without one of the country’s most promising young defenders. For now, Mbokazi will focus on surgery and rehabilitation before revisiting his ambitions of securing a move to Europe.

WHO SHOULD REPLACE HIM IN THE BAFANA BAFANA TEAM?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs star Baartman compared to Man United and Barcelona legend
World.content:
Former Cape Town Spurs coach Sean Connor has compared Kaizer Chiefs forward Luke Baartman to former Manchester United and Barcelona striker Henrik Larsson.

Connor handed Baartman his senior professional debut during their time together at Cape Town Spurs and believes the 20-year-old possesses the qualities needed to become a top striker.

The Irish coach praised Baartman’s movement, aggression and natural finishing ability, revealing that he was convinced of the youngster’s talent long before promoting him to the senior team.



Baartman impresses for Kaizer Chiefs

“I remember watching Luke Baartman every day with the Cape Town Spurs youth team,” Connor said.

“I loved his movement and his aggression. Then I went to watch him play for the DDC team, and the boy could finish. That’s when I realised he was a natural finisher.”

Connor said Baartman’s playing style reminded him of Larsson, one of Europe’s most intelligent forwards during his illustrious career.



“When I brought him into the first team, I even said to Luke, ‘Go and Google Henrik Larsson because I think you can play that type of striker.’

“I had spoken to Shaun Bartlett before about giving Luke an opportunity, but at that stage he probably felt Luke was still a bit too young.

“Then, when I was given the temporary reins, the very first thing I did was bring Luke into first-team training. 

“What convinced me even more was that he wasn’t timid. He was doing the same things I’d seen him do with the youth team,” he said as per GOAL.

Baartman joined Kaizer Chiefs last season but was limited to only a handful of appearances during his debut campaign.

The striker has started the new season on a positive note, earning the Man of the Match award in Chiefs‘ 1-0 victory over Kruger United. His performance has raised expectations that he could play a key role for Amakhosi in the months ahead.



What’s your take on Baartman?

World.title: DStv customers to lose access to four channels next month
World.content:
MultiChoice has confirmed four more DStv channels will be discontinued this year. Image: file / canva

DStv subscribers will lose another four channels next month as MultiChoice continues reshaping its television line-up to reflect changing viewing habits.

MultiChoice SA LicenceCo has confirmed that the four channels will stop broadcasting at 23:59 on 16 September 2026.

The company said programming from the discontinued channels will continue to be available elsewhere on the DStv platform.



Which channels are being removed?

The following channels will be discontinued:

M-Net Movies 1

kykNET Lekker

Mzansi Bioskop

Mzansi Music

According to Mybroadband, MultiChoice said the move forms part of an ongoing review of its channel portfolio.

The company said that instead of spreading similar content across numerous channels, it is focusing on fewer, stronger channels to create a simpler and easier-to-navigate viewing experience.

Eleven channels gone this year

With these latest closures, DStv will have removed 11 channels from its platform during 2026.

Earlier this year, BET Africa, CBS Reality, CBS Justice and MTV Base were discontinued after Paramount shut down its linear television operations in Africa.

The broadcaster also removed tlnovelas in January, then replacing it with Novelas+ in July.



Despite the reductions, some subscribers have also gained access to additional content. DStv Access customers, for example, received WWE, Trace Gospel and Trace Ngoma as part of the platform’s channel updates.

MultiChoice said it will continue reviewing and refining its channel offering as audience viewing habits evolve.

World.title: Rita Ora spotted aboard a yacht in Ibiza (Pics)
World.content:
Rita Ora, the British singer, songwriter, television personality and actress, spent the weekend in Ibiza.

The pop star spent the weekend soaking up the sun aboard a yacht in the Spanish party island, and her latest Instagram drop had fans talking for more reasons than one.

The photos, shared over the weekend, quickly made their way around entertainment pages, with plenty of people weighing in on more than just the scenery.



Rita Ora’s Ibiza yacht day, built for summer

Ora spent the afternoon aboard the boat in a black two-piece, styled with the kind of easy, no-fuss glamour that’s become her signature on holiday. One of her many Ibiza summer looks.

The look sparked plenty of comments from fans, many joking about the fit. Still, the mood of the day looked clearly relaxed rather than styled for the cameras.

This isn’t Ora’s first laid-back, deliberately undone holiday look, and it won’t be her last.



She has built a reputation for treating her downtime exactly like downtime. Fans comment on every detail regardless.

Ibiza’s moment in the sun this summer

Beyond Ora’s own trip, the yacht day fits neatly into this summer’s wider pattern of European celebrity holidays, with stars sailing around the Mediterranean’s most photographed coastlines one boat trip at a time.



Her stop in Ibiza puts her in good company, with the island remaining one of the season’s busiest celebrity hotspots.

Rita Ora has never once looked like she’s performing for the cameras, even when the whole internet is watching. That’s the real reason her Ibiza trips keep landing the way they do.

World.title: New twist in St Stithians tragedy as police open murder case
World.content:
St Stithians teenagers Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a Grade 11 learner, and Ethan Coetzee died at a lodge in Sabie. Police have since opened a murder case. Images: St Stithians

Police have opened a murder case following postmortem findings into the deaths of St Stithians teenagers Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a Grade 11 learner, and 19-year-old Ethan Coetzee, who were found dead at a lodge in Sabie, Mpumalanga.

Police respond to lodge

The South African Police Service (SAPS) said officers were called to the lodge on Monday, 3 August, at about 07:50 after reports that two people had been found dead.

When officers arrived, they found the bodies of a 19-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl. Both were declared dead at the scene.



Police initially registered an inquest docket.

Postmortem changes direction of investigation

The investigation took a new turn after the postmortem examination.

According to SAPS, the results suggest the 17-year-old girl may have been strangled, while the 19-year-old man may have taken his own life.

Police have since added a murder charge to the investigation.

“The postmortem results suggests that the 17-year-old female may have been strangled, while the 19-year-old male may have taken his own life,” SAPS said.

Investigation continues

Police said the investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the deaths.



On Tuesday, St Stithians College shared two separate posts about the tragic deaths of Ethan Coetzee and Cameron Waldeck-Cooks.
